tests/test_soul_path.py (80 lines)
  imports: from domain.inference import load_soul, save_soul, soul_path, soul_read_candidates
  -> domain/inference/soul_path.py      MISSING
  -> soul_read_candidates               0 hits anywhere in packages/core-py or domain/

packages/core-py/tests/test_compressed_transfer_wire.py (108 lines)
  imports: from domain.infrastructure.compressed_transfer import (...)
  -> domain/infrastructure/compressed_transfer.py  MISSING

Both were written ahead of their implementation (test-first, or against a
design that was abandoned/relocated). Either the module lands, or the tests
are deleted. They cannot be committed as-is.

=== ITEM 2 — the held-back test BLOCKS collection of its whole directory ===
Running packages/core-py/tests/ aborts at collection:
  ERROR collecting tests/test_compressed_transfer_wire.py
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'domain.infrastructure.compressed_transfer'
  -> Interrupted: 2 errors during collection

This is worse than a red test: ONE untracked file makes the entire
packages/core-py/tests/ suite unrunnable without --ignore. Anyone running the
directory gets a hard stop, not a failure count.

(second collector error was test_user_journeys.py -> ModuleNotFoundError:
 playwright, an env gap, unrelated to this card)

Workaround in use: --ignore=packages/core-py/tests/test_compressed_transfer_wire.py

=== ITEM 3 — test_notifications.py: needs an isolation ruling ===
Observed earlier: fails 7/21 in a full-suite run, but reproduces
identically at baseline (pre-existing, not caused by the services relocation).

Re-verified this session:
  - alone                         -> 26 passed
  - + test_pugqeep_checkpoint.py  -> 67 passed
  - + test_coverage_expansion.py  -> 72 passed

So it is NOT reproducible with those pairings. The polluter is some other
file in the directory. A full-directory run was started to bisect it but was
interrupted (server restart) before it produced results.

NEEDED DECISION (this is the actual ask):
  (a) find the polluting file and fix the leaked state (shared fixture /
      module-level singleton / event-loop reuse), or
  (b) mark it explicitly as order-dependent (pytest.mark.xfail or a
      documented skip reason) so the red is intentional and visible,
  or (c) declare the file hermetic-by-test and split the polluted cases out.
Do NOT just blanket-skip it — 7 unexplained reds train people to ignore red.

=== DONE WHEN ===
1. soul_path + compressed_transfer either implemented or tests deleted
2. packages/core-py/tests/ collects cleanly with NO --ignore needed
3. test_notifications has a written ruling (a/b/c) and no unexplained reds

NOT reproduce in any reachable environment. Evidence matrix (victim =
test_notifications, all on deterministic order, no randomly/xdist):

  3. root branch, tests/+cli EXECUTED then victim (inverted, worst case):

  4. root branch, 402-file core-py PREFIX executed + victim: GREEN

  5. root branch, full core-py collection (all ~700 modules imported) + only

Original "7/21" logs are NOT preserved (journal + evidence dirs searched;

5473eb90) all landed AFTER the observation; (ii) concurrent same-tree runs —

description:
ROOT-CAUSED 2026-10-04 (found while filing card 2656f858 — board stats printed both 'in_progress: 23' and 'in-progress: 3').

=== THE BUG ===
Board header declares exactly 4 columns:
  ['todo', 'in_progress', 'review', 'done']        (store.py:123, kanban.py:47)

3 cards sit in a 5th column that was never declared: 'in-progress' (hyphen).

  fdedff96-d22c-4475-8974-3472033bb811   Recover job_1438982c (paste-journey-live @99%) + fix runtime config persist
  20260929_073_product_docs_truthup      Product docs truth-up (PRODUCT_ENGINEERING/ROADMAP/FEATURES/INDEX) + guard
  20260929_075_quickstart_truthup        QUICKSTART.md + root entry docs truth-up + guard (seam 6)

=== IMPACT: they are silently invisible ===
Board rendering iterates HEADER columns (store.py load_board -> board.columns),
not the columns discovered from cards. Proof:

  board show | grep 'Recover job_1438982c'     -> no match
  board show | grep 'Product docs truth-up'    -> no match
  board show | grep 'QUICKSTART.md + root'     -> no match
  board show renders 919 lines, IN_PROGRESS header shows only the 3 valid cards

get_stats() DOES discover them (by_column is built from cards), which is why
'board stats' prints 'in-progress: 3' while 'board show' renders none of them.
Two views of the same file disagree — stats counts a card the UI cannot show.

=== WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT ===
Validation exists ONLY on the CLI path:
  cli.py:191-193  if args.column not in valid_columns: print(...); return 1
That guards 'app-planner move <id> <col>' — an interactive command.

load_board() (store.py:263-272) does NO validation. It accepts any record with
'id' + 'title' and passes column through untouched via Card.from_dict
(store.py:61-77, column=d.get('column','todo')). So a hand-edited line — or
any writer that bypasses move_card() — lands silently.

Card.from_dict has no column check either.

=== WHERE IT CAME FROM ===
git log -S'"column": "in-progress"' -- .kanban/board.jsonl
  60b64c1b9 (2026-09-23)  FIRST introduction
  parent 110bca236 has count=0 -> this commit added it
  0758ed1d5    (2026-09-29)  'add cards 078-087 + restore card 075' -> count 0->3

The introducing hunk is a hand-authored line, not produced by add_card/move_card:
  +{"id": "openrouter-provider-wiring-01", ..., "status": "in_progress",
    "column": "in-progress", ...}
Note it wrote BOTH 'status' (snake, correct) and 'column' (hyphen, wrong) in the
same record — a human/agent typing the English hyphenated form directly into
JSONL. grep across *.py/*.ts/*.tsx/*.js/*.sh finds NO writer of the hyphenated
column value anywhere — it never came from code.

=== ALSO OBSERVED: notes are gone, so sync will never repair these ===
All 3 matching notes are absent from notes.journal.jsonl ('NO NOTE' for each).
sync_from_notes (store.py ~515) matches by TITLE against existing notes; with
no note it never calls move_card, so these 3 stay in the phantom column forever.
They cannot self-heal.

=== PROPOSED FIX (pick one) ===
A. Validate at the boundary (right fix): in load_board(), warn on unknown
   column and either coerce to 'todo' or record it in a report. load_board is
   the single choke point every reader goes through — cli.py:191 already has
   the valid-columns list, so the check already exists, just not on this path.
   Defense belongs on READ for a file that is hand-editable.
B. Repair the 3 cards: move to a real column (likely 'done' — all 3 are
   2026-09-29 work; 2 are 'docs truth-up + guard' seams). One-off, does not
   prevent recurrence.
C. Make stats and show agree: get_stats() should bucket unknown columns as
   'other' (or validate) so the two views stop disagreeing.

Recommend A + B together; C follows from A. Do NOT only do B — the file is
hand-edited by design (kanban jsonl), so without A a next typo hides cards
again silently.

=== DONE WHEN ===
1. load_board() rejects/reports an undeclared column
2. the 3 cards are in a declared column (or deliberately deleted)
3. board show and board stats report the same card count
4. a test asserts every card's column is in the declared set
RESOLUTION (2026-10-08) — LANDED on main: 91e81243b.
Card drifted between root-cause (2026-10-04) and pickup: DONE-WHEN 2 was
already satisfied (the 3 phantom 'in-progress' cards now sit in 'wip' —
verified, not touched by this session), write paths already reject retired
spellings (67c406ee2 validate_column), and C follows automatically because
get_stats() reads load_board(). Open work was fix A + tests (DONE-WHEN 1/4).
SHIPPED: load_board() now coerces an undeclared column to the fallback
('todo', else first declared) with a logger.warning naming the card, the
spelling, and the declared set — coerced, never dropped, so the card becomes
visible and consistently counted; validate_column() docstring updated (its
'Reads are untouched' claim became false). 4 new tests (TestReadPathColumn-
Validation): coerce visibility, warning content, stats/load agreement with a
phantom present, and a recurrence guard asserting every card of the REAL
.kanban/board.jsonl is in the declared set — that last one would have caught
the original 3-card bug. GATES: RED 3 failed -> GREEN 198 passed (full
app-planner suite); ruff + py_compile clean. DONE-WHEN proven on the real
board: board show renders 966 card lines == stats Total 966, buckets 842/77/
32/15 all in vocabulary; no other suite imports app_planner.

description:
Source: one-by-one infra review 9-13 (apps/api/server/infrastructure/). Approved via user 'fix and all' + 'build everything into our code' (2026-10-04). EXCLUDED (parked): gateway Phases 1-3, trusted-edge design, 10 profiler feed-or-retire decision, mogdb history-store swap (separate card), undecoded 'insights' ask.

P0 DEADLOCK (startup_history.py:374+379): get_optimization_suggestions acquires self._lock (threading.Lock) then calls get_stage_stats which re-acquires the same NON-reentrant lock; health.startup_history async handler (routers/health.py:226) thus blocks the uvicorn event loop forever on first request. Fix: threading.RLock or snapshot-then-compute outside the lock.

MISSING FINALIZERS - one wiring point at end of boot (startup.py) currently calls NONE: (a) staged_loader finish_history() zero callers -> 9 history never appended/committed; (b) viz.finish() zero callers -> terminal summary never prints; (c) only STARTUP_START emitted at startup.py:359 - STARTUP_COMPLETE/STAGE_COMPLETE/HOOK_FAILED never fire. Wire finish_history + viz.finish + STARTUP_COMPLETE together at end of boot (after READY).

9 P2: finish_startup imports get_metrics (does not exist) -> swallowed ImportError every time; use get_metrics_collector. 9 P3: _save_to_disk open(w)+json.dump non-atomic -> tmp+os.replace. 9 P4: docstring calls nonexistent record_startup(); fix docstring.

11 P2: delete dead code - terminal_hook (0 callers), _move_up/_clear_line (0 callers), _printed_count (never read), line 128 discarded expression; fix docstring (CM yields None into 'as hook').

12 P2: emit() awaited inline in boot path (startup.py:359) -> a slow registered webhook could add ~32s to boot; fire-and-forget with asyncio.create_task. (WebhookStore consolidation deferred to its own card.)

13 compression.py: P0 gzip.compress runs synchronously ON the event loop -> await asyncio.to_thread (matches new AGENTS.md execution-philosophy: async seam); P1 body += chunk O(n^2) -> list + b''.join; P2 max-size cap (skip-to-identity above ~8MB, symmetric to gateway MIN_COMPRESS_BYTES); P3 accept-encoding substring treats 'gzip;q=0' as accept; P4 Vary only set on compressed path; P5 rebuilt responses: drop stale content-length/transfer-encoding, add pre-compressed skip-list entries (x-xz/bzip2/zstd).

ACCEPTANCE: (1) PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 + PYTHONPATH=packages/downcraft:packages/core-py:apps/api/server conda pytest on startup/health/compression tests green; (2) py_compile touched files; (3) health JSON shapes unchanged; (4) new tests: suggestions endpoint cannot deadlock + boot-end wiring fires finish_history/viz.finish/STARTUP_COMPLETE exactly once; (5) branch fix/startup-finalizers; preserve pre-existing dirty .kanban/.dev-notes files (do not revert other sessions work).

WHAT: apps/api/server/infrastructure/startup_history.py persists via full-file JSON rewrite (SLO_STARTUP_HISTORY_PATH or ~/.slogpt/startup_history.json). Swap to a MogDB collection following the feedback-controller house pattern (data/feedback_mogdb): db dir data/startup_history_mogdb, one doc per record, create_sorted_index(timestamp).

- finish_startup -> collection.insert_one(record.to_dict()) + prune to max_records (keep newest)
- constructor loads newest max_records sorted by timestamp desc
- clear_history -> collection.drop() + in-memory clear
- lazy import with sys.path insert of packages/mogdb/src (apps/cli/src/groups/db.py pattern) so it works regardless of launch PYTHONPATH; on ImportError/open failure degrade to in-memory with one warning - observability must never fail boot (WebhookStore degraded-mode pattern)
- legacy JSON: if present, migrate records once (skip timestamps already present) then rename to .bak - never delete user data; SLO_STARTUP_HISTORY_PATH becomes the legacy-source env var, document it in docs/ENVIRONMENT.md (currently undocumented)
- constructor: persist_path param -> db_path (only callers are tests/server/test_startup_finalizers.py - update the 3 sites + persistence test); add migration + degraded-mode tests; add startup-history as consumer example in docs/mogdb-guide.md

ACCEPT: health JSON shapes unchanged (routers/health.py startup_history); targeted suites green (test_startup_finalizers, test_startup_routers, health tests); ruff + py_compile clean; no duplicate docs (edit existing); reuses shared packages/mogdb copy (no new venv/node_modules).

PATTERN DOC LANDED: docs/TRANSPORT_PROJECTIONS.md (registered in docs/INDEX.md; cross-linked from the docs/routers.md header and the Router Playbook in PRODUCT_ENGINEERING.md). Doctrine stays in root AGENTS.md Endpoint & Transport Rule — this card is the build half.

THE WORK (status after implementation):
1. `create_router(spec, route, handler)` — emits real route fragments from a ToolSpec descriptor: verb derived from idempotency (idempotent -> GET, action -> POST, explicit override logged), 422 contract violations, success_response envelope, classify_and_raise errors, auth_scope -> require_auth_if_enabled, OpenAPI operation with x-contract. Lives in apps/api/server/infrastructure/contract.py (server/web side only; domain stays capability-only, no FastAPI import).
2. Boot self-registration — routers/_manifest.py GENERATED by scripts/gen_router_manifest.py (order-preserving: Starlette matches in registration order; main.py-registered health/consciousness/status/dashboard excluded by parsing main.py itself); `--check` fails CI when stale. Lazy import + failure isolation untouched: 53 routers / 555 routes / ~1.8s cold set load.
3. CI contract gate — scripts/check_contract.py: descriptor literals + registry-vs-served-route cross-check BLOCKING; route-baseline diff (apps/api/server/contract-baseline.json) and hand-written duplicates REPORT-ONLY. scripts/check_docs_api_parity.py extended to parse create_router (AST) so projected routes participate in parity.
4. TS projection: generate typed helpers for http-client.ts instead of hand-writing each endpoint. Coord card 656023ab (http-client modularization) owns the host module. NOT done on this card.
5. Pilot: brand-new `GET /contracts` router (routers/contracts.py) — the contract registry's own read path, descriptor-backed, no migration of existing routers. External utility tier: operator/introspection surface, NEVER entering the model-visible tool registry (domain/tools, the inference UI).

GUARDRAILS: no god endpoint (a POST /tools/{name} switchyard is the other wrong answer, not the fix); one envelope, one auth story, one versioning story; the 57 existing routers are grandfathered — migrate only when touched (Router Playbook rule 5).

New crossing named here (rule 1): `GET /contracts` — read-only contract-descriptor inventory served by the new pilot router (the registry's own read path; consumed later by the TS projection + OpenAPI contract diff). Not model-facing, never enters the chat/agent tool registry (tier rule 4).

Decisions 2026-10-04: helper named `create_router(...)` (user), pilot = brand-new router (no migration of existing routers), CI = descriptor check blocking + OpenAPI diff report-only, boot self-registration = generated manifest (`routers/_manifest.py`) with CI diff.

COORDINATION 2026-10-04 06:16 — PARALLEL IMPLEMENTATION, resolve before merging: second session committed 77fbbb817 (branch feat/create-router-projection, root checkout) 54s AFTER fa7f62eb6 merged create_router to main and 3s before push 8074dc475. Different design (resolve_method, 222-line contract.py, test_contract_projection.py) vs merged (derive_method + registry + generated manifest + contract CI, 35 tests). Both add apps/api/server/infrastructure/contract.py -> their merge will conflict. Main is the shared copy: build on create_router there; rebase 77fbbb817 onto 8074dc475, keep only what the merged design lacks, retire the duplicate file.
**RECONCILIATION GUIDE 2026-10-04 06:2x (for the `feat/create-router-projection` session).** Their branch now duplicates BOTH halves of this card — `77fbbb817` (`contract.py`, 222 L) and `37112a9f9` (mount table: `_manifest.py` + `gen_router_manifest.py` + `routers/__init__.py` + parity-script edits). Six files collide with what is already on `main` (`7ee2b8c0c`), so the merge is guaranteed to conflict: `infrastructure/contract.py`, `routers/_manifest.py`, `routers/__init__.py`, `scripts/gen_router_manifest.py`, `scripts/check_docs_api_parity.py`, `docs/TRANSPORT_PROJECTIONS.md`.

*Equivalence map (theirs -> already on main):* `resolve_method(spec, override)` -> `derive_method(spec)` + explicit `RouteSpec.method=` that is **logged** (drift visibility is the documented decision); `build_request_model(spec)` -> `_request_model(spec)` (private, JSON-Schema -> Pydantic, 422 contract violations); `check_handler_matches(spec, handler)` -> `_check_handler_accepts(spec, handler)`; `ROUTER_MODULES` tuple -> same symbol, same file, 53 modules in preserved historical order.

*What main has that theirs does not (stop building these):* `ContractRegistry`/`RouteEntry` + `REGISTRY` cross-check, envelope + `auth_scope` + error classification per projected route, `_openapi_extra` (descriptor params published to OpenAPI), the pilot `GET /contracts`, the `contract-gate` CI job (static+runtime blocking, route/**OpenAPI-operation** baseline report-only over 491 operations), docs truth-up (`AGENTS.md`, `TRANSPORT_PROJECTIONS`, `routers.md`, `API.md` 607/58), and 35 passing contract tests. CI proof: `Contract gate` green on both my pushes; `test-server` FAILED-set byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (112 lines, zero mine).

*What theirs has that main lacks — port these instead of re-implementing:* (1) `check_pre_lifespan()` + `_has_module_router()` in `gen_router_manifest.py` — a "every manifest entry actually mounts an HTTP router" assertion main does not have (main excludes main.py-registered modules by parsing `main.py`; theirs verifies mounted-ness — complementary, keep theirs); (2) `tests/server/test_router_manifest.py` (98 L) — keep if it adds cases beyond `test_contracts.py::test_router_manifest_is_fresh`; (3) drop the legacy `_router_names` dual-source regex check — `_router_names` no longer exists on main, so it is dead; (4) resolve `check_docs_api_parity.py` in favour of main's AST version (theirs is regex and misses `RouteSpec(...)` first-arg-less forms).

description:
User directive 2026-10-04: build this as a FEATURE first, then project to consumers (endpoint/UI, CLI). My earlier proposal (patch apps/cli core/validator.py directly) was consumer-first and was rejected — that's why the CLI doctor, the API and the UI never agree.

## Inventory (main, 2026-10-04)

- Core EXISTS: `domain/core/_internal/doctor/` (Phase A `729210a48`): probe registry `probes/{http,journey,sse}.py`, models (findings + severity triage), `report.py` -> `~/.cache/slog-doctor/findings-report.json` (`$SLO_DOCTOR_REPORT`), `__main__.py` entry. Tests: `packages/core-py/tests/test_doctor.py` (650 lines).
- API EXISTS: `apps/api/server/routers/doctor.py` — `GET /doctor/report`, `POST /doctor/run` (landed `40ba857e0`, card `6d0ebf37`).
- UI EXISTS: `apps/web/app/(app)/doctor/page.tsx` + `components/doctor/` (DoctorSummary, FindingsList, ComponentHealthStrip, RunDoctorButton).
- CLI DISCONNECTED: `cli.py system doctor` runs the old `apps/cli/src/core/validator.py` Doctor (python/dirs/pkgs/disk/accel/API/.env) — shares nothing with the core, and no surface anywhere reports thermal/load/uptime.

## Gap

No system/environment probes: thermal, load average, reboot/uptime. Plus the CLI never consumes the shared core/report.

## Plan (feature -> contract -> consumers)

1. Core: `probes/system.py` — thermal (same sensor source `scripts/benchmark_latency.py` reads; warn >=85C, fail >=95C), system load (`psutil.getloadavg()` vs cpu_count; warn >0.7x, fail >1.5x), uptime/boot time (warn if uptime <30min = recently rebooted). Register in `probes/__init__.py` (one registry entry = the contract).
2. TDD: RED test first (`packages/core-py/tests/test_doctor_system.py`), then GREEN.
3. CLI projection: `cli.py system doctor` delegates to the doctor core (report/run), validator checks stay as their own section or fold in — one core, two views.
4. Use it: one doctor run produces the artifact evidencing the environmental (thermal/load) caveat for card `df5affc7` latency benchmark (+67% with the benchmark's own `thermal ok=False`).

## Acceptance

- Probe tests RED -> GREEN; existing `test_doctor.py` stays green; ruff clean.
- Doctor run emits system findings (thermal/load/uptime) in the report consumed by `GET /doctor/report` (UI needs no change beyond inheriting).
- CLI surfaces the same core.
- External-utility tier (b): registered in the execution layer, NEVER in the chat/agent tool registry.
- df5affc7 note references the artifact.
title: Doctor core: system-health probes (thermal/load/uptime) + CLI projection — feature-first

description:
ROOT CAUSE (systematic-debugging, verified 2026-10-04): domain/infrastructure/_internal/lifecycle.py types StartupHook.handler / ShutdownHook.handler as Callable[[], Awaitable[Any]] -- docstring says "Async callable. Receives no arguments." Every invocation site does await asyncio.wait_for(h.handler(), ...). Health GATES are the sync contract (Callable[[], bool], called not awaited) -- that split is correct and intentional.

PRODUCTION IS CLEAN (verified, not a prod bug): all 8 startup phase handlers (_phase_task_queue/_phase_config/_phase2_model_load/_phase3_wandb/_phase4_multimodal/_phase5_model_registry/_phase6_routers/_phase_ready) and all 9 shutdown handlers in apps/api/server/infrastructure/startup.py are async def; register_gate lambdas are sync. No contract violation at runtime.

THE BUG IS IN THE TESTS -- 4 sites in packages/core-py/tests/test_lifecycle_extended.py pass non-awaitables:
1. line 363 lambda: (order.append("a"), asyncio.sleep(0)) returns a TUPLE -> TypeError -> hook a (critical) fails -> b/c depend on a -> never run -> ValueError: 'b' is not in list. THIS IS THE VISIBLE FAILURE (test_startup_dependency_order).
2. line 365 same (hook b), 3. line 368 same (hook c).
4. line 484 handler=lambda: ran.append(True) returns None -> PASSES BY ACCIDENT: the append executes before wait_for raises TypeError, and test_shutdown_runs_hooks only asserts the side effect, never hook success. Latent -- masks a failed hook.

VERIFIED NOT A MAINLINE BUG: test_lifecycle_extended.py and lifecycle.py are byte-identical to main (diffed); only conftest deltas differ and they are unrelated thread-teardown fixtures. So failure 1 reproduces on main too. The OTHER failure in the run (test_lifecycle.py::test_string_representation) is ALREADY FIXED on main by 1bd574d4d / card 20260924_050 -- this branch feat/webhook-consolidation is 230 ahead / 259 behind main (forked 2026-09-25) and predates it.

FIX (test-only, no production code): rewrite the 4 handlers as async def that append then await asyncio.sleep(0). Keep assertions unchanged. RED already observed; GREEN = the 11-file infra set (664 passed baseline, 2 failed) goes to 666 passed / 0 failed.

SHARED WORKSPACE
- index updated: no index change required (test-only fix; no new app/package/doc)
- shared copy reused: conda sloughgpt python + existing PYTHONPATH; zero installs, no new node_modules/.venv
- coordination named: build OFF MAIN in an isolated worktree so the user's dirty feat/webhook-consolidation checkout (staged pytest.ini pythonpath fix, modified pugqeep/engine.py, 3 untracked test files) is never touched. Related closed cards: 20260924_050 (StrEnum assertion, main), 20260809_001451_resolve-infra-test-blockers (earlier infra blockers). Open card 20260924_031_sync-session-feedback-batch and 20260929_071 own tests/server + routers, not these files.

description:
Two competing pytest.ini files + 55 duplicate test basenames make test results depend on WHICH ARGS YOU PASS — the same code collects differently under different invocations.

=== PART 1 — two competing pytest.ini files (the habitat) ===
Repo has two ini files with divergent settings:

  KEY           packages/core-py/pytest.ini        root pytest.ini
  -----------   -------------------------------    -----------------------------------
  testpaths     tests                              packages/core-py/tests tests apps/cli/tests
  pythonpath    . ../mogdb/src ../downcraft        (WAS ABSENT — added in 4ad4072d9)
                ../chargectl/src ../.. ../../apps/api/server
  addopts       -q -m "not slow"                   -v --tb=short -m "not slow"
                --ignore=tests/test_neural_e2e.py  --import-mode=importlib
  markers       slow, integration                  unit, integration, e2e, slow

pytest picks ONE configfile: the nearest ini to the COMMON ANCESTOR of the
args passed.

  pytest packages/core-py/tests/test_X.py   -> rootdir = packages/core-py  -> INNER ini
  pytest tests/foo.py packages/core-py/...  -> rootdir = <repo root>       -> ROOT ini
  pytest  (no args, uses testpaths)         -> rootdir = <repo root>       -> ROOT ini

So the SAME test file runs under two different configurations depending on
what else is on the command line. Before 4ad4072d9 the root ini had no
pythonpath key at all, so any root-level arg silently dropped
mogdb/chargectl/downcraft from sys.path and broke collection — that was the
actual cause of the "test_notifications fails 7/21 only in full suites"
mystery (see card 64bb9214 ITEM 3; it was never test pollution).

=== PART 2 — 55 duplicate test basenames (the residual) ===
55 test basenames exist in BOTH packages/core-py/tests/ AND another test
dir, with NO __init__.py in any of them:

  tests/              17 files
  tests/server/       37 files
  apps/cli/tests/      1 file  (test_permissions.py)
                     ------
                      55 total

Under --import-mode=importlib both copies resolve to the same module name,
so one shadows the other:

  ERROR collecting packages/core-py/tests/test_training_pipeline.py
    ... is not the same as the test file we want to collect:
        /home/mana/.../sloughGPT/tests/test_training_pipeline.py
  HINT: remove __pycache__ / .pyc files and/or use a unique basename

The pairs are genuinely DIFFERENT files, not symlinks:
  test_training_pipeline   root=5585   core=17253
  test_quantization        root=10190  core=74557
  test_rag                 root=8152   core=15615
  test_vector_store        root=3023   core=38192

Which one dies depends on ARG ORDER (arg order decides the winner), so
these pairs are effectively half-collected in every full run.

CURRENT FULL-COLLECTION TALLY (after 4ad4072d9):
  56 errors total, 45110 tests collected
    53  <- duplicate-basename collisions (this card)
      3 <- known, NOT this card:
             packages/core-py/tests/test_compressed_transfer_wire.py (held back, 2656f858)
             tests/test_soul_path.py                                  (held back, 2656f858)
             packages/core-py/tests/test_user_journeys.py             (needs playwright)
  Before 4ad4072d9 it was 83 errors / 43902 collected.

NOTE ON A COMMIT-MESSAGE INACCURACY: 4ad4072d9's message says "17 duplicate
test basenames shared between tests/ and packages/core-py/tests/". That
undercounted — the true figure is 55 across three dirs (tests/, tests/server/,
apps/cli/tests/). The commit could not be amended: the other session landed
c9cbd280c on top of it, and amending would have rewritten their unpushed
commit. Treat this card as the corrected record.

=== WHY IT MATTERS ===
Test outcomes are a function of the command line, not of the code. A dev
running one file sees green; CI running the suite sees red (or vice versa).
53 errors is ~100% of the current collection-error budget — nothing else
is failing to collect.

=== PROPOSED FIX (not started — needs a decision) ===
Option A — dedupe the basenames (55 renames). Rename the packages/core-py
copy or the tests/ copy so every module name is globally unique.
  + root cause gone, no import-semantics change
  - 55 renames across 3 dirs; must not break references/discovery

Option B — add __init__.py to all four test dirs. Makes them packages, so
importlib derives distinct module names from the full path.
  + tiny change (4 files)
  - changes import semantics for EVERY test module; highest blast radius,
    needs a full-collection A/B (83/56 baseline is already recorded above)

Option C — unify the two ini files into one at the repo root, so invocations
stop diverging at all.
  + eliminates Part 1's habitat entirely
  - root vs inner addopts differ (-v vs -q, --import-mode); inner --ignore
    and testpaths must be reconciled; must prove core-only runs unaffected

Suggested order: C first (kills the divergence that hid this for weeks),
then A (clears the 53). B alone would clear the 53 without fixing the
divergence that caused the original 28-error mogdb failure.

=== DONE WHEN ===
1. Part 1: root-only vs core-only invocations give identical results for the
   same test file (today they can differ)
2. Part 2: 53 duplicate-basename collection errors reach 0
3. Full `pytest` collection runs with 0 errors and no --ignore workarounds
   (remaining 3 must clear too: 2 held-back tests per card 2656f858, plus
   playwright availability)

Baseline evidence for A/B comparisons lives in the 4ad4072d9 commit message
and in card 64bb9214.

--- COORDINATION SCREEN 2026-10-09 (opencode triage lane) — DO NOT START YET ---
The proposed fix (C then A) is already in flight on another machine's
ACTIVE branch stack, unlanded:
  dcb2a5eaf "test: consolidate four test roots into a single tests/ root"
    (packages/core-py/tests -> tests/core-py, 826 files) — kills Part 2's
    55 duplicate basenames structurally (option A+B combined);
  a7f7d541a "mirror packages/core-py/pytest.ini onto root's behaviour" — Part 1;
  8ec57d606 "--continue-on-collection-errors" (workaround, not the fix);
  4ad4072d9 "root pytest.ini gains pythonpath" (partial content already on
    main: packages/mogdb/src only).
Branches carrying the stack are LIVE (cave-game-vm, vm-asm-intake,
fix/phantom-conftest-import, fix/restore-metrics-router all committed
2026-10-09). Renames on main today = guaranteed conflict with their
826-file move. Wait for that stack to land, then re-measure this card's
DONE-WHEN (collection errors may already be ~0). Pending-commit screen by
opencode triage lane; card left in todo deliberately.


--- claimed 2026-10-11: Gene batch — PART 1 via cherry-pick f2cc0ee0a (one pytest config, root ini only); PART 2 duplicate-basename inventory to follow. Worktree .wt-gene-pytestcfg, branch test/pytest-cfg-d2803a3c. ---

--- PART 1 CLOSED 2026-10-11 (Gene batch 3, finished inline after Gene's
4th infra death) — landed 14ccda235 on origin/main (port of stranded
f2cc0ee0a from fix/pytest-single-config, applied cleanly) ---
packages/core-py/pytest.ini deleted; root pytest.ini is the single source —
its pythonpath is the union of both sets (root-relative) and it carries the
nested --ignore=packages/core-py/tests/test_neural_e2e.py in root-relative
form. The python_functions = test_* key was REMOVED (it would have silently
dropped 37 camelCase tests: 36 in test_shell_repl_more.py + 1 in
test_lm_eval_char.py — the nested ini never set it, so pytest's default
test* collected them). VERIFIED on this tree: plain `pytest` from
packages/core-py/ (CI's invocation) and from repo root now resolve to the
SAME configfile (root pytest.ini, pyproject.toml warning identical both
ways) and collect IDENTICALLY: 42541/43062 collected, 521 deselected (was:
two different inis with divergent addopts/timeout/pythonpath/filterwarnings).
Execution parity: test_train_pipeline.py 161 passed (from packages/core-py,
plain pytest) + repo-root tests/test_api_keys.py 21 passed — matching the
source commit's own verification counts. STILL RECORDED, NOT CHANGED:
pyproject.toml carries a third [tool.pytest.ini_options] block repeating
python_functions = ["test_*"] — deleting pytest.ini would resurrect the
37-test loss; pyproject is hot shared territory.
PART 2 (55 duplicate test basenames) SPLIT OFF to follow-up card
dup-testnames-01 — inventory + recommendation recorded there; the original
invocation-dependent-collection risk is defused by PART 1 (one config +
--import-mode=importlib everywhere), so the rename sweep is now hygiene,
not a correctness fix. [PART 2 follow-up card: d79237cd-5bf5-]
notes: coordination 2026-10-08 (ca167dbd closed): root pytest.ini received ONLY the keys 'timeout = 120' + 'timeout_method = signal' (+ comment). No other settings touched; two-pytest.ini consolidation + duplicate basename work remains THIS card's scope.

description:
Source: infra review 10 feed-or-retire, decided FEED via evidence on user 'continue' (session pattern: figure-it-out delegation). Branch: feat/startup-profiler-feed (stacked on feat/webhook-consolidation).

EVIDENCE FOR FEED OVER RETIRE: two consumers exist (health.startup_export 'profile' key + health.startup_profile which promises 'per-hook timing ... identifying bottlenecks') and a producer exists (staged_loader.run_stage opens/closes stages), but profile_hook has ZERO callers - every stage reports hook_count=0, duration=0, slowest=''. Retire would strip a health JSON key or delete a documented endpoint = forbidden shape change.

PLAN: (1) wrap ONLY 'await asyncio.wait_for(hook(), ...)' in _run_hook with profiler.profile_hook(name) - wrapping the whole try/except would make swallowed failures report success=True; profile_hook error becomes str(e) or type(e).__name__ so bare TimeoutError reads 'TimeoutError'. (2) get_summary() must stop calling finish(): finish() clears the OPEN stage, so a health call during boot silently drops in-flight hook timings (latent race the feed makes live) - compute summary from stages non-mutating instead. (3) wire profiler.finish() as an isolated finalizer in _finalize_startup so profile.to_dict() top-level totals (total_hooks/total_success/total_failure, set ONLY by finish(), which has zero callers) become real. (4) add module-level profile_hook() convenience - the module docstring advertises 'from infrastructure.startup_profiler import profile_hook' which currently fails (only a method exists). (5) remove write-only racy _current_hook slot (3 write sites, 0 readers; hooks profile concurrently via gather).

MUST NOT TOUCH: health endpoint JSON shapes, staged_loader metrics-collector/history/rollback paths, terminal viz.

ACCEPT: new tests/server/test_startup_profiler_feed.py (run_stage records success/failure/timeout hooks; get_summary non-mutating keeps open stage alive; module-level import; finalizer sets totals); existing tests/server/test_startup_finalizers.py green; full tests/server vs baseline 7; ruff+py_compile clean.
title: Feed per-hook timings into the startup profiler (review 10)

description:
PROBLEM (from user screenshot): VoiceChatMode center stage stacks FOUR visuals in a column -- ListeningIndicator rings, VoiceWaveform (32 bars, 280x80), ListeningBars, then VoiceOrb wrapping the mic button. On screen that reads as a stray hairline + a small button with nothing anchoring the view.

APPROACH (expert-reviewed, user said continue): one hero orb is the single presentation surface for the voice state machine already owned by useVoiceChat (idle|listening|processing|speaking|error).

1. VoiceWaveform.tsx -- grow VoiceOrb into the hero (~200px): token-driven layered glows via color-mix(), listening = mic-level reactive scale + corona rings, processing = slow orbit ring, speaking = outward ripples, idle = quiet, error = border-destructive. Extract ONE shared stateTone() map so the header status dot and the orb cannot drift apart (state->color is currently hardcoded twice).
2. VoiceChatMode.tsx -- orb-only center stage: drop the stacked VoiceWaveform/ListeningBars/ListeningIndicator, keep the exact existing toggle button (handleToggle, disabled=isProcessing, same aria-label) inside the orb. Header, footer, transcript, settings, interim/final text, error StatusBanner unchanged.
3. Level plumbing: mic level is produced by a rAF loop in createAudioLevelMonitor -> onLevel -> setMicLevel, i.e. React re-renders the whole overlay ~60x/sec to move transforms. Write --mic-level onto the orb element imperatively and let CSS consume it in transform/opacity; React state carries only the discrete VoiceState.

description:
Extends the hazard class of card df5affc7 (SubprocessProcess fork -> forkserver).

## Evidence (2026-10-04, run 8)

- Full-gate run #1 FROZEN 02:56:37 at 88% (index 37821 = packages/core-py/tests/test_vector_backend.py region): parent pytest in do_wait, children showing parent cmdline, futex_do_wait = run-7 signature.
- ISOLATED REPRO: `pytest test_vae.py test_vector_backend.py --timeout=90` freezes identically (98/112, parent do_wait, workers futex; SIGTERM could not unwedge).
- Mechanism: vector_backend.py:109 `mp.Pool(_N_PROC)` = bare default context = FORK on py3.12; test_vae's OpenBLAS threads live in the pytest process at fork -> fork-into-multithreaded worker deadlock; first `pool.map` blocks the parent in waitpid forever.
- NOT a forkserver regression: vector_backend.py untouched by feat/pugqeep-forkserver. Sweep: this is the ONLY bare Pool in production code (rest is ThreadPoolExecutor = no fork).

## Plan (approved via session continue, 2026-10-04)

1. `mp.get_context(_pool_start_method()).Pool(_N_PROC)`; default forkserver (spawn on win32), escape hatch env `SLO_VECTOR_START_METHOD=fork` (mirrors pugqeep config.start_method + SLO_* env convention).
2. TDD: RED tests on pool start method (context default + env escape + helper), then GREEN; existing 20 numerics tests = behavioral guard (they also stop wedging).
3. No forkserver preload changes (would clobber pugqeep engine's preload invariant) — cold-start cost measured instead by new `scripts/benchmark_vector_backend_pool.py` (fork vs forkserver: construction->first-dispatch latency + steady dispatch throughput).
4. Acceptance: test_vector_backend.py full green with NO hang; benchmark recorded; full packages/core-py/tests gate re-run for df5affc7 acceptance; then ask user before merge.

## Notes

- Workers are module-level (`_matmul_worker` etc.) over SHM-name tuples -> already forkserver-compatible; fork was the only inheritance-dependent piece.
- VectorBE construction happens per-model-load (SLNC path), not per-request -> worker cold-start amortizes.

description:
Found 2026-10-04 by scripts/benchmark_vector_backend_pool.py (card a0ba949b).

## Evidence

- Hundreds of `multiprocessing.resource_tracker: UserWarning: '/psm_<uuid>': [Errno 2] No such file or directory` lines at process exit after any run that constructs VectorBE and dispatches through the pool (826 warnings on the fork-only benchmark arm — reproduced with BOTH start methods, so it is orthogonal to the fork->forkserver change).
- Mechanism (py3.12): each worker's `shm.SharedMemory(name=...)` ATTACH registers the segment with the resource tracker (gh-82344 class); `VectorBE.__del__` then unlinks segments manually; at exit the tracker re-unlinks already-gone names and warns, once per registration (same name repeated for N workers).
- Cosmetic only — no data loss, no functional impact; pytest hides it (warnings filter), raw script runs show the flood.

## Scope

- Affects: `domain/infrastructure/_internal/vector_backend.py` shm lifecycle (`_shm_blocks` create/unlink) + worker attach path.
- Candidate fixes: unregister after manual unlink (py3.13 `resource_tracker.unregister` is private in 3.12 — verify), stop worker-side registration on attach (3.13 behavior), or centralize shm lifecycle in a small manager that owns create/unlink with matching tracker calls.
- Must not: change the SHM sharing contract (workers read via name), or break fork AND forkserver contexts.

## Acceptance

- Benchmark/test runs exit with zero resource_tracker warnings; no leaked /dev/shm segments (check `ls /dev/shm` after runs); both start methods green.

RESOLUTION (2026-10-08) — LANDED on main: f5ccd713a.
ROOT CAUSE (proven with a tracker-pid probe, not assumed): VectorBE constructed
the Pool BEFORE any shm op, so fork-arm workers forked before the tree's tracker
existed -> each started its OWN tracker (parent pid X vs worker pid X+1,
SHARED=False) -> worker attach registrations (weights + unique per-dispatch out
names) accumulated in per-worker caches -> parent unlinked files first ->
worker-exit sweeps hit ENOENT. Measured RED: fork arm 214 resource_tracker
lines (99 Errno 2 + 8 'leaked' notices, 16 names in one worker's cache);
forkserver arm 0 lines on this machine (it already shares via spawn prep
tracker_fd) — the card's 'both start methods' claim did not reproduce here.
FIX (2 sites, worker fns untouched): (1) resource_tracker.ensure_running()
before Pool construction -> one shared tracker, worker attaches dedup against
the creator's entries; (2) __del__ FileNotFoundError fallback unregisters
block._name (stdlib unlink() runs shm_unlink BEFORE unregister without
try/finally — a gone file would skip the unregister) + _shm_blocks.clear()
for idempotence (double-unregister KeyErrors the tracker cache.remove(),
measured: traceback in tracker child). Rejected: worker-side unregister — on
the shared tracker it would pop the creator's entry and break exactly-once.
GATES: fork arm 214 -> 0 lines (stderr 0 bytes, same args); both arms
iters=10 = 0 warnings; /dev/shm empty; timings stable (steady matmul
29.6ms vs 37.4ms RED — no regression); test_vector_backend 24 passed
(fork path exercised by the benchmark subprocess; suite is ctx-level for fork
by design); ruff + py_compile clean. Acceptance met: zero warnings, no leaked
segments, both start methods green, sharing contract unchanged.
title: Cleanup: resource_tracker '/psm_*' warning spam on VectorBE teardown (py3.12 shm attach/register)

Expert review concluded the algorithm is sound but the hosting is not: the C FFI `transformer_forward_step(w, cache, token_id, seq_pos, logits)` takes ONE token at ONE position, so block decoding needs a new C primitive. WHAT IS BROKEN (verified 2026-10-04, conda sloughgpt, PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1):
  from domain.inference._internal.native import bindings; bindings._find_lib()
    -> RuntimeError: libtransformer_forward.dylib not found. Compile with:
       cc -O3 -march=native -dynamiclib -framework Accelerate -o libtransformer_forward.dylib ...
  Only a macOS Mach-O `libtransformer_forward.dylib` is committed on main.
  No `.so` anywhere in tree. So the native engine is UNLOADABLE on this Linux box.

GOOD NEWS - the source is ALREADY portable. domain/inference/_internal/native/transformer_forward.c:
  line 15  #ifdef __APPLE__
  line 16  #include <Accelerate/Accelerate.h>
  line 18  /* Portable BLAS: link with -lblas on Linux/BSD. Values match standard cblas.h. */
  line 20  void cblas_sgemm(...)      <- hand-rolled forward decl, not <cblas.h>
  line 30  static void sgemm_t(...)   <- single wrapper, 10 call sites (137,138,139,160,167,168,172,296)
So this is a BUILD + LINK task, not a rewrite. bindings.py already lists
`libtransformer_forward.so` as a candidate — only the compile hint is macOS-locked.

PLAN:
1. Build libtransformer_forward.so on Linux (cc -O3 -march=native -shared -fPIC, -lblas/-lopenblas, -lm).
   Decide whether the hand-rolled cblas_sgemm decl should become a real <cblas.h> include.

4. Add a repeatable build entrypoint (scripts/ or Makefile target) so the artifact is reproducible, not a mystery binary.

description:
Found while driving the main default test gate green (card cbd2ffc3), 2026-10-04. The online LoRA feedback loop is dead in production:
- get_online_lora_updater() (domain/feedback/_internal/online_train.py:340) builds OnlineLoRAUpdater() with engine=None, and self.engine is only ever assigned in __init__ — there is no attach/setter path, so no caller ever supplies an engine.
- _compute_gradients (line 173) returns {} immediately when self.engine is None.
- _perform_update then calls _apply_gradients({}) — a no-op — yet still increments total_updates / total_samples, stamps last_update_time and logs "Updated with N samples". Telemetry reports updates that changed nothing.
- Second defect: even WITH an engine, _apply_gradients does self._lora_weights["W_a"] -= grad, where W_a is (rank=8, dim=768) but gradients["W_a"] is seeded from np.zeros_like(grad) and accumulates grad.mean(axis=0), giving shape (seq, vocab) — a broadcast mismatch that raises and is swallowed by the outer try/except ("Update failed").
- The only branch that ever populates W_b is the pseudo-gradient exception fallback, which applies random noise to live weights.
DECIDE: either wire an engine (real feature work: shape-correct gradients for both W_a and W_b) or retire / mark the capability not-implemented so callers stop counting phantom updates.
Note: tests/test_feedback_domain.py gradient tests were re-pointed at a stub engine in cbd2ffc3; they assert CURRENT behaviour, not the desired end state.
RESOLUTION (2026-10-08) — LANDED on main: 93286c6fe.
DECIDE resolved to RETIRE (option b) — evidence: apply_to_logits has ZERO
production callers (tests only), so even a wired engine would never reach
inference; and engine backprop would need hidden-state access the engine
interface (text.encode + forward->logits) does not expose. Wiring = separate
feature card if wanted. WHAT SHIPPED: (1) honest accounting — _perform_update
only moves total_updates/total_samples/last_update_time when
_apply_gradients actually changed weights; otherwise
total_skipped_updates/total_skipped_samples + INFO skip log (the 'Updated with
N samples' phantom telemetry is gone); (2) _apply_gradients returns the applied
key count and SKIPS shape-mismatched gradients instead of raising into the
swallow (defect 2); (3) pseudo-gradient random-noise fallback RETIRED (defect 5
— it mutated live weights with noise); (4) get_stats() + docstrings mark the
capability not-implemented (engine_attached flag). Tests: 16 new/retargeted
across test_online_lora/test_online_train/test_feedback_domain — including 4
baseline-red tests that asserted gradients-from-nothing, now green under the
honest contract. The thread-safety invariant now counts applied+skipped+
buffered (it previously depended on phantom counting). GATES: RED 8+3 -> GREEN
273 passed across 6 files (online_lora, online_train, feedback_domain,
feedback_controller, workflow_router, quality_guard); ruff + py_compile clean;
frontend has 0 consumers of these keys; no new baseline ids.

description:
Follows card 1228d061 (Linux build port, commit 25cd0a369). Its own NEXT-FEATURE CANDIDATES listed two perf levers. MEASURED BOTH BEFORE BUILDING — the disciplined version of "continue building".

BASELINE (scripts/benchmark_native_transformer.py, -O3, warmup2/rep9 median, same box):
  tiny  (L2 D16 V512):   prefill 14789.5 tok/s, decode 8000.0 tok/s
  small (L6 D128 V4096): prefill   273.1 tok/s, decode  259.1 tok/s
  Earlier runs on a busier box read ~2x lower — cross-session numbers are NOT comparable, only same-session A/B is.

LEVER 2 — hoist the per-step malloc/free: KILLED BY MEASUREMENT.
  Actual count is 7 + 2*n_layers per token, NOT 7. forward_layer mallocs "normed" every
  layer (transformer_forward.c:133) and gqa_attention mallocs "scores" every layer (:89).
  small = 19 malloc + 19 free per token. At ~30ns each that is ~1.1us against a
  3860us/token budget = 0.03%. Not worth touching. Do NOT build it.

LEVER 1 — better GEMM/GEMV: partially live.
  All 8 call sites pass sgemm_t(M=1, ...) so these are GEMVs, never GEMMs. Microbench at our
  exact shapes (8 shapes x 6 layers + lm_head, 8.00 MB read/token):
      sgemm(M=1) [current]  1.00x
      cblas_sgemv           1.02x   <- switching primitive is WORTHLESS here
      plain dot loop        1.20x
      restrict + ivdep      1.17x
      restrict + unroll4    3.64x   <- THE WIN (4 independent accumulators)
  Reference netlib BLAS does not special-case M=1, which is why the hand-rolled 4-way
  accumulator beats it 3.64x. Current rate = 2.80 GB/s against 8 MB/token, so the ceiling
  from GEMM work alone is roughly 550-700 tok/s on "small".

LEVER 1b — OpenBLAS: BLOCKED, needs owner approval to unblock.
  No OpenBLAS/ATLAS/MKL on the system (ldconfig: only libblas.so.3).
  numpy/scipy DO bundle one but it is scipy_-prefixed (scipy_cblas_sgemm,
  scipy_cblas_sgemm64_) and a hashed private copy -> BOTH link probes FAILED.
  Getting a real OpenBLAS means an install, which the shared-workspace rule forbids
  without asking. ESTIMATED UPSIDE: 2-3x on decode. Owner call.

WHAT THIS CARD BUILDS: built-in GEMV kernel as the default on non-Apple, making the .so
dependency-free (no cblas.h, no -lblas dev symlink, no probing) — which also removes the
whole class of problem card 1228d061 had to probe around. External BLAS stays available as
an opt-in (SLO_BLAS=... plus -DSLO_HAVE_CBLAS) for anyone who has OpenBLAS. The change is
confined to sgemm_t; semantics preserved (C = A*B^T, alpha=1, beta=0, lda=ldb=K, ldc=N —
verified against CBLAS row-major rules, and M stays general so a future M>1 call is correct).

GATE BEFORE COMMIT: test_native_engine_real + test_ct_provider must stay 71 passed / 1
skipped green (fp summation ORDER changes, so outputs may shift), ruff/bash clean, and an
A/B benchmark of builtin vs system libblas on BOTH presets.

SHARED WORKSPACE: no installs, no new venv/node_modules, conda sloughgpt only.
Coordination: builds on 1228d061; unrelated to d6519c8f / 56cf354c / 89de1db1.
title: Native forward perf pass: built-in GEMV kernel replaces netlib BLAS (3.6x) — levers measured, 2 of 3 killed

FIX DIRECTIONS (user selected this as the next unit of work): (a) point the CI e2e job at the Vite path the config intends (npm run e2e:vite / dev server on 5173) — likely flips most specs without app changes; or (b) mount the react-router Router provider during Next SSR (or guard the shim). Verify by running the full 21 specs green.

Evidence: gh run view 37271817846 --log-failed (and 37274567586). Main has no required checks; E2E red did not block the #122 merge (user approved).

description:
Decision (2026-10-17): user picked 'sockets first, then requests' after expert review — build our own minimal wire, then host the FastAPI app-object contract on it; uvicorn remains default host until gates green.

Grounding from review:
- App contract = FastAPI app object (host-agnostic; uvicorn swap surface = uvicorn.run + two dev.py argv).
- WS endpoint exists: apps/api/server/routers/inference.py:1569 ws_generate (needs RFC6455 handshake + text frames, or uvicorn stays default until done).
- SSE via StreamingResponse (apps/api/server/training/sse_stream.py) — wire must stream chunked.
- SelectiveGZip + CORSMiddleware are app-level (Starlette) — sit above any host, no reimplementation.
- PGQ owns the control-plane wire already (framed socketpair + os.fork); HTTP wire is the unowned gap.
- Execution philosophy: wire core stays SYNC (threads); asyncio confined to the ASGI-host adapter module; explicit seam queue-in/async-write-out.

Phases:
1) packages/wire-py — stdlib-only sync TCP accept loop + HTTP/1.1 framing (parser/serializer, keep-alive, chunked, malformed->400, header caps); pytest framing suite.
2) request/response layer — ASGI host adapter on the wire (wire/asgi_host.py); minimal WS for ws_generate; SSE streaming path.
3) verification — A/B curl harness vs uvicorn (status/headers/body equality), scripts/benchmark_transport.py (p50/p95 latency, throughput, SSE TTFB, WS echo), journey gates; SLO_TRANSPORT=wire env flag; default flip only when all green.

Side findings this session (separate cards): slo dev API lifespan hangs at startup hooks in worktree (log 17:28:21: 'PGQ engine stopped', 'InferencePool shut down' while uvicorn waits for application startup; also startup writes data/+logs/ → dev.py 'python -m uvicorn --reload' has NO --reload-excludes → reload-loop hazard; main.py --reload path has them).

Open: placement (packages/wire-py vs apps/api/server/transport), WS in v1 or deferred (default flip gated on WS either way).
title: server-infra: own the wire (sockets) layer first, then request/response layer on top

DEFECT (found by cleanup-agent sweep 2026-10-19): tests/test_code_hygiene.py::test_no_bare_except is RED against a tree with ZERO real bare excepts. BARE_EXCEPT = re.compile(r'except\\s*:') + line_hits() is a line-oriented TEXT scan, so it matches prose: domain/infrastructure/_internal/atomic_write.py:7 is a module-docstring sentence ('...because the except: unlink tail is the part people forget').

The gate is wrong in BOTH directions:
- noisy: matches docstrings/comments/future prose -> false reds
- leaky: misses 'except :' (legal whitespace) and 'except\\n:' split across lines (legal) -> real bare handlers pass unseen

FIX: measure the thing, not the glyph. Rewrite test_no_bare_except as an AST walk flagging ast.ExceptHandler nodes with type is None (ast already imported and used in this file by _main_guard_ranges). Failure format stays rel:lineno: source line. Files that do not parse become FAILURES, not silent skips. Drop now-unused BARE_EXCEPT (2 refs, both in this file).

REJECTED: (a) rewording the docstring to dodge the regex - degrades accurate docs to appease a dumb scanner, and that phrase is what a reader greps to learn why the module exists; (b) adding a file exemption - blinds the scanner to a future REAL bare except in that file, i.e. silencing, which the file header forbids ('never silence').

GATES: pytest tests/test_code_hygiene.py -> 4 passed (was 1 failed, 3 passed); ruff check + ruff format --check on the test; other 3 tests unaffected. Scope of sweep: 2366 .py + 2143 .ts/.tsx files, GNU grep (rg not installed on this machine).

description:
SOURCE: deferred from the chat-engine-port lane (branch feat/chat-engine-port, commits 83aeac8a0 stream-first refactor + aad552524 cancel-channel fix). Cancel was fixed first because it is correctness; this is a dropped FEATURE and was explicitly split off as a separate card.

DIAGNOSIS
The stream-first refactor moved POST /chat/stream onto stream_turn via ChatRouter._stream_tokens. The handler it replaced (InferenceRouter.chat_stream, ~997 lines in apps/api/server/routers/inference.py) maintained a reconnect cache:

  - on partial response (GeneratorExit / client disconnect): set_chat_response_cache(session_id, {tokens, complete: False})
  - on completion: set_chat_response_cache(session_id, {tokens, complete: True})
  - at connect: get_chat_response_cache(session_id) -> if present, _chunk_replay(cached) replays the already-generated text and returns WITHOUT re-generating

The new path calls none of them.

IMPACT
apps/web/lib/stream-chat-response.ts runs a for(;;) retry loop and re-POSTs /chat/stream on failure/reconnect. With no cache, a reconnect regenerates the whole turn from scratch: duplicate token cost, non-idempotent, and the user sees the answer restart. _chunk_replay is already written for this (replay concatenates back to the exact cached text, whitespace included) and is still used by /inference/generate/stream at inference.py:1402.

IMPORTANT — event-id replay is a trap, and it always was
_frontend sends lastEventId, but no handler ever emits SSE id: — sse_event() accepts an id= param that the token framing never passes (sse_fallback.sse_token -> sse_event(..., message="")), and _event_counter only ever went to logs/cache. So Last-Event-ID cannot drive this. Replay must stay keyed on session_id exactly as the old path did, unless this card also adds real event ids to the frames (and then the frontend path must be verified to honour them). Decide explicitly; do not assume the frontend contract works.

EVIDENCE (re-run to confirm still true)
  grep -n "set_chat_response_cache\|get_chat_response_cache" apps/api/server/routers/chat.py   -> 0 matches
  same grep on apps/api/server/routers/inference.py -> only lines 306/318 (defs) + 1934/2515/2653/2664, all on the now-unreferenced chat_stream path

OWNED PATHS (this card may touch only these)
  - apps/api/server/routers/chat.py
  - apps/api/server/routers/inference.py (cache helpers at ~306-330; do NOT touch stream_turn/turn registration beyond what the cache needs)
  - tests/server/test_chat_state_seam.py or a new tests/server test
Must-not-touch: domain/ (the port stays app-import-free; caching is an edge concern), and the chat_stream/handle_chat_stream retirement (separate card).

DEFINITION OF DONE
  1. POST /chat/stream stores the partial on disconnect and the full text on completion.
  2. A second POST /chat/stream for a session with a complete cache replays it and does NOT call provider.chat_stream again.
  3. A test pins (2) by asserting provider.chat_stream is never invoked on the replay path.
  4. Gates green: ruff check <paths>, scripts/check_contract.py --static, scripts/check_docs_api_parity.py, tests/server suite.

PORT-DON'T-REBUILD
Replay machinery already exists: _chunk_replay + get/set_chat_response_cache in inference.py. Reuse it; do not write a second cache.

SCOPE QUESTION FOR THE FOREMAN
Verify against docs/PRODUCT_ENGINEERING.md and docs/UX_FLOWS.md that stream-reconnect is a real journey before building (Page Rule 5-point test logic applies to features too). If reconnect is not a persona task, the right move may be to drop the replay requirement and instead make the frontend retry idempotent. Do not silently pick one.
title: chat: restore /chat/stream reconnect replay dropped by the stream-first refactor (deferred from chat-engine-port)

description:
## Root causes (diagnosed, approved)
1. `apps/web/vite/next-compat/navigation.ts:51` — `router.refresh()` shim is `window.location.reload()`.
2. Direct `window.location.reload()` sites IN SCOPE: developer r-shortcut (:62), vm r-shortcut (:580), tokenizer onRetry (:77), benchmark onRetry (:194), companion onRetry (:132), StatusBar handleRetry success (:83), CommandPalette clear-chat (:77), useLiveStatus checkReload after 6 health failures (:367, redundant — SSE reconnects with infinite backoff + fallback poll).
3. Latent trap: `lib/cache/client.ts` `invalidateQuery` only sets `updatedAt: 0`; mounted `useQuery` views do NOT refetch (fetch effect deps are `[sk, enabled]`) → invalidation alone is a no-op. Needs a `refreshVersion` bump.
4. Good existing machinery (reuse, do NOT rebuild): `lib/cache/client.ts` (fetchQuery/invalidateQuery/subscribe, dedup, staleTime/GC on zustand useQueryStore), `lib/cache/hooks.ts` (useQuery w/ refetch, useMutation + invalidateKeys, useInvalidate), per-page `useRefreshShortcut(fetchData)`.

## Fix shape
A. client.ts: `refreshVersion` (init 0) + `revalidateAll()` (mark every entry `updatedAt: 0`, keep data/error/status and in-flight `_promise`; bump version). Export from barrel.
B. hooks.ts useQuery: read `refreshVersion`; `lastVersionRef` first-seen; extend fetch effect deps; on advance, if enabled and no in-flight `_promise`, force `fetchQuery` — previous data stays, `isLoading` stays false (no spinner flash).
C. navigation.ts: `refresh = useCallback(() => revalidateAll(), [])`.
D. Pages: tokenizer/benchmark/companion onRetry → their own refetch/loader; developer r-shortcut → page loaders or `refreshKey` remount of active tab; vm → extract initial idempotent GET loads into `loadVmData` useCallback (never touch training timers, *Touched refs, form state); StatusBar handleRetry → `revalidateAll()` after successful health; CommandPalette clear-chat → deleteKV + `revalidateAll()` + reuse existing chat store reset if one exists.
E. useLiveStatus: `checkReload` → revalidate semantics (`MAX_FAILURES_BEFORE_REVALIDATE`, `revalidateAll()`, status 'connecting', failureCount 0, log `health_revalidate_threshold`); delete document reload, sessionStorage loop-guard (`slo-reload-count`, `slo-reload-window-start`), delay timer, unused RELOAD_* constants (grep first). Keep 'reloading' status member.

## DoD
- [ ] No `window.location.reload()` at any of the 8 in-scope sites; `router.refresh()` no longer reloads the document.
- [ ] `revalidateAll()` exists + exported; mounted useQuery refetches on version bump with `isLoading` false while cached data exists.
- [ ] vm/user input state (training timers, *Touched refs, source/maxSteps/role/trainConfig form) survives an `r` refresh.
- [ ] Tests: lib/cache/hooks.test.ts (2 cases), vite/next-compat/navigation.test.ts (no location.reload + version/stale assertion), any test asserting old reload behavior updated.
- [ ] Gates: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run lint` (or proven pre-existing red on origin/main); vitest on touched files + full apps/web suite (flake: /valence/i — rerun once, else prove pre-existing).
- [ ] PR opened (root causes, fix shape, test plan) + checks run to completion; AGENT_SYNC appended; note -> review, board moved. NO merge, NO card close.
title: Web app feel: revalidate state instead of full-page reload

description:
EXPOSED 2026-10-20 by the prod any-burn-down (cards 8345b255): typing the
consciousness pages against the real API showed the episode-history contract
is a lie the tests' mock fixtures hide.

CONTRACT TRUTH
- GET /consciousness/history/episodes returns exactly 5 keys:
  timestamp, input_text, self_insight, growth_delta, qualia
  (apps/api/server/routers/consciousness.py:297-304).
- Domain SelfEpisode has 6 fields: timestamp, input_text, response, qualia,
  self_insight, growth_delta (domain/cognition/_internal/consciousness/
  self_model.py:69-77). There is NO rating field and NO episode narrative
  field ANYWHERE in the domain. get_stats guards hasattr(ep, 'rating')
  (consciousness.py:1096) which is always False.
- Test fixtures declare input/response/rating/narrative anyway — mock-vs-
  contract drift, which is exactly what ruling card d715327c would catch.

DEAD READS (all pre-existing, now typed/being typed)
- history/page.tsx: truncate(ep.input) L405 renders undefined; search L142-144
  over input/response/narrative never matches; StarRating L414 always empty;
  response/narrative blocks L419-428 never render.
- master/page.tsx L213-225: rating distribution + averages always 0.
- analytics/page.tsx L201/228: ratings chart empty (filter r>0).
- statistics/page.tsx L249: avgRating always 0.
- playground/page.tsx L319: star variant never activates.

FEEDBACK TARGETING BUG (playground)
- L307 realIndex = ep.index ?? 0 but the endpoint NEVER sends `index`
  (grep router "index": 0 hits) -> realIndex is 0 for every card ->
  duplicate React keys, "#0" labels, and handleFeedback(0, r) -> backend
  indexes the FULL list (consciousness.py:400-405), so every star rating
  mutates global episode 0. Correct mapping exists: total is already
  returned (line 307); global index for reversed display position d =
  total - 1 - d.
- history/page.tsx has the same realIndex pattern (L414).

RATINGS ARE NEVER PERSISTED
- submit_feedback (consciousness.py:393-419) only recomputes growth_delta and
  beliefs; the rating itself is discarded. Even a payload fix cannot show
  ratings without a domain field + persistence.

ALSO IN THIS AREA (fixed by the slice commit, listed for completeness)
- statistics L238 treated epoch-seconds as ms (new Date(ts) without *1000)
  -> episodes-per-day was always episodes.length. Fixed in the same commit.

NEEDS A USER RULING before code — do not silently pick one:
(a) RESTORE THE FEATURE: extend the history payload (response + input alias
    are free — domain has them), add a rating field to SelfEpisode with
    persistence, decide what episode narrative means (product: derive from
    self_insight?), fix feedback indexing = total - 1 - d. Real work,
    domain + router + pages + tests.
(b) CUT THE DEAD UI: remove star ratings and narrative blocks, narrow search
    to input_text, map input -> input_text; keeps UI honest with what the
    engine stores; rating feature returns later with persistence behind it.
(c) MIXED: free payload additions now (response + input alias), defer the
    rating-persistence product decision separately.
Recommendation: (c) — the payload lines cost nothing and un-break input/
response/search immediately; rating deserves its own product call because
it changes what the engine remembers.
title: consciousness episodes: UI reads fields /history/episodes never sends — rating/input/search/feedback targeting dead — NEEDS RULING

description:
MEASURED 2026-10-20 on the merged landing-chain tree (and reproduced on origin/main): **4 failures in 30 solo runs (~13%)**. It also failed once inside a full `pytest tests/ -m "not slow"` run, then passed on an identical re-run of the same tree (3340 passed) — i.e. a random red that will make any landing session look like it broke something.

ROOT CAUSE (both halves verified by reading the code):
1. `domain/training/_internal/chat_trainer.py:565` — `eos = 0`, and `generate_from_chat_model` does `if eos in out_ids: out_ids = out_ids[:out_ids.index(eos)]`, then returns the slice AFTER the prompt. So a single sampled EOS at step 0 yields `out_ids[len(tokens):] == []` -> returns `""`.
2. `train_chat_model(pairs, config, on_step, cancel_event)` takes **no seed/rng parameter at all**, so the test cannot make the run deterministic. Its siblings in the same file DO seed what they can (`np.random.default_rng(0)` at lines 68/78/294) — this one has nothing to seed.
3. The assertion is only `isinstance(output, str)` + `len(output) > 0`, so an empty-but-valid generation fails it.

PROPOSED FIX (needs a ruling — it is outside the 4 cards currently in review):
(a) preferred, no API change: seed the global RNGs at the top of the test (`np.random.seed(0)`, and `torch.manual_seed(0)` if the model init uses torch), matching the file's own convention; and

`packages/core-py/tests/test_signal_communication.py::TestEpisodicMemory::test_recall_negative_k`

- 10-16 `2e1bceb17` `fix(shell): recall(k<0) fails closed in both memory classes (card dc74ec04)` — implementation docstring reads 'k == 0 returns all; k < 0 returns none', code does `if k < 0: return []`, and `test_shell_memory.py:143` pins it: 'k < 0 is invalid input and fails closed (returns []), for BOTH classes and BOTH by_reward branches. Negative k returning the whole buffer was a silent-unbounded footgun'.
- 10-18 `0b8980207` `test(sweep): 12F singles batch G ... (card 621fcd57)` rewrote the pin: `- assert result == []` → `+ assert len(result) == 1`, with a comment claiming 'k <= 0 is the documented return-all episodes contract, pinned by test_shell_memory.py (both the k == 0 and the k < 0 cases)'.
- That citation is false: the very test it cites pins the opposite, and the sibling `test_recall_negative_k_by_reward` (line 933) still asserts `== []`. So origin/main's suite asserts both sides of the contract; only the flipped one fails, because it is the only one the implementation contradicts.

### Fix (this card)
Restore `assert result == []` and replace the mis-citing comment with the true contract + provenance (fix 2e1bceb17 / card dc74ec04; regression from 0b8980207). No production code changes — `domain/shell/_internal/memory.py` is already correct.

## Remaining clusters (characterization in flight)

description:
## Finding (from CI-red lane card bdda0736, cluster 4)
`Point.accuracy`'s contract is [0,1], and `explained_accuracy()` (commit 1be3eaaec) now clamps at all 6 producers — but the clamp only treats the SYMPTOM. The real defect: nearest-centroid assignment uses `np.searchsorted(centers, x, side='left')` = **ceiling lookup, not nearest**.

Evidence: degenerate row `token_emb::71` = 13×0 + 0.9999975 + −0.002249 + 5.975798e-10 → the near-zero element lands in the ≈1.0 cluster (ceiling of its own value region) → mse≈1/16 > var 0.0586 → accuracy −0.0664 (pre-clamp). Bit-identical at np.seed 62 full-run; direct repro seeds 200/240/243.

## Why it needs its own card
Fixing assignment semantics (true nearest-neighbor over centers, tie-breaking rules) changes **cluster membership** → mse/var/accuracy/PSNR for every mixed row → compression ratios, quality floors, possibly benchmark verdicts. Blast radius far too large for the CI-red lane (which only had to restore the [0,1] contract).

## Scope sketch (to refine at intake)
- Assignment: nearest by L2 (or per current center metric) with deterministic ties; keep `searchsorted` only as the sorted-index fast path with a ±1 neighbor check.
- Re-baseline: run `scripts/benchmark_quantization.py --quick --tiny` before/after; expect ratio shifts only on mixed rows.
- Pins: existing TestAccuracyContract rows must stay [0,1]; add a mixed-row pin asserting the NEAREST cluster (not ceiling).
title: pugqeep nearest-centroid is NOT nearest: searchsorted ceiling mis-assigns mixed rows — clamp treats the symptom (finding of bdda0736)

## Agreed design — "AML cruncher" data pipeline
Goal: actual WEIGHT-TRAINING datasets (not the knowledge store/RAG — user drew this line explicitly) feeding SloughGPTTrainer, so the model learns rather than being a pass-through dataset query engine.

Decisions:
1. Pipeline: import (8 existing sources: local/github/hf/url/kaggle/csv/batch/isbn) → clean (MinHash/LSH dedup + quality filter + PII scrub — NOT SIFT/SURF, those are image-only) → immutable versioned snapshot → dataset adapter → SloughGPTTrainer (NO new training loops — AGENTS.md consolidation rule) → eval gate → merge.
2. "Live learning" = staged offline batches (clean→snapshot→LoRA/adapter→eval gate→merge), never continuous gradient writes; snapshot immutability = bad data pack rolls back by version, never corrupts the running model.
3. Cruncher name = AML (reuse packages/aml, Automatic Markup Language — typed @-blocks; ModalitySequence = @stream blocks with modality tag + pair links). Cruncher runs offline at ingest time, not inference time.
4. Modality order: text first (generic high-quality open corpora: Wikipedia, Stack Exchange, open books/papers; quality-over-quantity for embedded scale) → voice adapter (wrap existing phoneme encoder domain/multimodal/_internal/tts.py) → image/binary adapters (binary via pugqeep Huffman compressor). Modalities are first-class domains, not bolt-ons; cognition orchestrates.
5. Domain scope: GENERAL. Medical = future knowledge-pack riding the same pipeline (fruit-fly→full progression), not now.
6. Scale target: minimal/embedded (SBCs, small devices) — streaming incremental ingest, compact snapshots, model-likeness filtering (small SloNet can't waste capacity on junk tokens).
7. Open question (blocking build): does "all devices run" include on-device TRAINING, or inference only? Decides whether the cruncher needs a resource-budgeted mode.

Build order when unblocked: (1) ModalitySequence schema (AML blocks) + cruncher interface crunch(raw)->[ModialSequence]; (2) three adapters: text/voice/binary; (3) feed via existing dataset adapter → SloughGPTTrainer; (4) eval gate per modality.
title: PARKED: AML cruncher data pipeline — training datasets via clean→snapshot→adapter→eval-gate (text first, general domain, embedded scale)

Diagnosis (2026-10-23, from main run 39700451976 job 119575456419 — pre-existing, NOT caused by PR #174; same failure on 2026-10-21 runs 39587601511 / 39577178587):

Main CI/CD `build` job (docker buildx, apps/web/Dockerfile) fails:
  #7 [internal] load build context  transferring context: 2B 0.1s done
  #8 [deps 3/7] COPY packages/strui/package.json ...
  #8 ERROR: failed to calculate checksum of ref ... "/packages/strui/package.json": not found

Root cause: root .dockerignore contains these three lines (added in d9d500b02, 2026-07-16 "fix: model load 23s→5s..."):
  packages/strui/
  apps/web/
  apps/cli/
They exclude EXACTLY the trees apps/web/Dockerfile COPYs from (deps stage copies packages/strui/* and apps/web/* package manifests). The build context reaches buildx nearly empty, so every COPY of repo source fails.

Fix: remove/replace the three blanket excludes with junk-only excludes that still shrink the context, e.g.:
  **/node_modules
  apps/web/.next
  apps/web/.vitest-cache
  coverage
(patternmatcher walks parents: `apps/web/` excludes the whole tree; plain `node_modules` only matches root-level, hence the original over-exclusion motivation.)

Verification: docker buildx build --file apps/web/Dockerfile . must at least pass the deps stage COPYs (full local build may be heavy — workflow_dispatch / push-to-main CI/CD run is the real gate; note `build` job SKIPS on PRs so this cannot be validated on a PR branch).

Scope: .dockerignore only. Must not change Dockerfiles or workflow YAML. Card created during PR #175 finish-up; main's test-core-py is green post-#174 — this build job is the ONLY remaining red on main.


CLOSED 2026-11-03: fixed by 5210bddb4 (exact prescribed diff: dropped packages/strui/ apps/web/ apps/cli/ blanket excludes, added **/node_modules + apps/web/.next + apps/web/dist-vite) — ancestor of main; COPY-set check confirms every source passes.
title: fix(docker): .dockerignore excludes COPY sources — main CI/CD build job red (since d9d500b02)

description: DIAGNOSIS (2026-10-23): _apply_meta_weights (apps/api/server/routers/inference.py:347-444) merges the cached feedback nudge as value+nudge with NO clamp. Request schema bounds: temperature [0,2], top_p [0,1], top_k [0,500] int, repetition_penalty [0.5,2] (:298-301). Example: top_p default 1.0 + nudge 0.05 = 1.05 > le=1.0 -> downstream provider schema rejection; top_k 40 + (-35.0) = 5.0 float -> int-field type error; temperature/rep_penalty can drift out of range the same way. Explicit params (model_fields_set) pass through verbatim — pydantic already validated them; clamp applies ONLY to nudged (non-explicit) values.
title: fix(inference): clamp meta-weight nudges to request-schema bounds (top_p 1.05 > le=1.0)

description: DIAGNOSIS (2026-10-23): domain/infrastructure/_internal/model_worker.py line ~22: 'from __future__ import annotations' sits INSIDE the module docstring (between 'Architecture::' and the ASCII diagram) — it is text, not an import. Annotations are therefore eager. mp.Queue is a bound method (not a type), so 'mp.Queue | None' raises TypeError at runtime. 5 sites: nested _stream defs at :385 (SloNet worker spawn — the preferred path) and :659 (HF worker spawn) evaluate at def-execution = child-process start; 'self._req_q/_resp_q/_hb_q: mp.Queue | None' at :806-808 evaluate at ModelWorkerProcess instantiation. Import of the module itself succeeds (nested defs lazy), which is why this survived until worker spawn/instantiation. Fix: move the future import to a real module-level statement (single-point fix, all annotations become lazy strings). AST test guards the invariant (future import must be a real module-level statement, not docstring text).
title: fix(worker): real from __future__ import annotations — docstring copy left mp.Queue | None eager (TypeError at spawn)

Class = loading-state race under CI worker reuse, NOT the http-client mock family.

Evidence it is flake, not a real break: (1) failing PR #186 diff = 2 Dockerfiles + scripts/check_dockerignore.py + AGENT_SYNC.md — zero vitest surface; (2) same PR run 40076529521: ci.yml Frontend unit tests PASS, only ci_cd test-web FAIL; (3) main run 40001305458 test-web green (only build failed); (4) local repro in exact CI tree (sim of workspace-root npm ci of root lockfile) = 14/14 passed x3 consecutive runs; (5) worktree-local vitest cannot even resolve react (shares main checkout node_modules) — CI tree only repros via the sim.

Real fix = make the test await the loaded state (findByRole/await waitFor on the post-load trigger button, or assert within the loading transition) — do NOT just widen timeouts; if the page genuinely never resolves without mocked data, the mock promise is resolving late/never under reuse. description:
SYMPTOM: Browser VM panel shows red "VM Error" with "this.V86Class is not a constructor" (screenshot from user, Developer > Terminal > Browser VM).

ROOT CAUSE (traced, not guessed):
1. vite.config.ts:51 aliases /^v86$/ -> lib/node-builtin-stub.ts, an EMPTY stub (export default {}, no named exports). Same alias in next.config.js:40 (turbopack.resolveAlias browser condition).
2. v86-controller.ts:35-36 does await import("v86") -> receives the stub; fallback chain mod.V86 || mod.default?.V86 || mod falls through to the MODULE NAMESPACE OBJECT itself (not a constructor).
