description:
ARCHITECTURE COMPOSITION RECORD (user ruling, 2026-10-27): workspace is a SPACE, not a UI feature and not a user attribute. The app must be instantiable as whole-app processes (cells), with domain/business logic contained, and inter-process data exchange as typed events — so N workspace-instances can run side by side.

THE DESIGN (three layers, one ruling):
1. CELLS (instantiation): one cell = one workspace = one whole-app process. Workspace lives ONLY in an InstanceConfig composition root handed to boot (ports, state/session dirs, model ref); engines/routers/chat stay cell-unaware (zero per-workspace branches). Supervisor = control plane ONLY (slo instance up/down/list, port lock, restart backoff, aggregated health into the existing health/event stream) — never in the data path. 1 cell = today's app = the default zero-config path (no regression).
2. CONTAINMENT (failure domain): containment boundary == fault boundary == the process. Shared root cannot take siblings down; cell death = degraded-in-stream + restart, never cascade. Dependency rule already holds: domain logic inward, HTTP/SSE/CLI are projections of the contract.
3. EVENTS (inter-process data): events carry FACTS/state transitions, never request/response choreography (temporal coupling, unowned timeouts). Inside a cell = function calls across the async/sync seam; between existing processes = PGQ frames; between cells = almost nothing (edge routes, cell answers). ONE typed envelope {type, schema_version, occurred_at, correlation_id, payload} standardized on the EXISTING PGQ/pipe + health/event stream — no new bus, no broker, no external dependency (build-from-scratch-first: the only stdlib collaborator left is ThreadPoolExecutor).

COMPOSES EXISTING CARDS (do NOT create parallel cards — reconcile into this):
- ecea49c8 (todo): own the wire (sockets) layer, then request/response on top -> inter-process data transactions.
- 8fe718f5 (review): bounded execution stack + framing protocol (remove multiprocessing) -> event framing.
- 9fc4b4cf (wip): fault containment Tier-1 (shared root can't take the system down) -> containment invariant.
- NEW: InstanceConfig composition root + slo instance supervisor (this card's step 2-3).
- Reconcile with 2cec0811 (workspace-search landing, approved) BEFORE moving any workspace routing.

MUST-NOT-TOUCH: domain/** engines (stay sync, cell-unaware); single-instance deployment stays default; web UI only DEMOTED to a thin switcher (workspace stops being a page family — matches the existing "workspace is a philosophy, not a page" ruling + page-baseline ratchet; the 4 /workspace/* knownWorkspaceNamespace nav routes are pin-gated — any change goes through apps/web/lib/page-journey-gate.test.ts); no gateway resurrection (ux-012c: gateway is dead infra); no UI redesign in this card.

STEPS: 1) this composition record; 2) InstanceConfig dataclass threaded through boot only (env reads collapse to one derivation in config.py); 3) supervisor in CLI + port lock file; 4) event envelope schema on existing PGQ/pipe + correlation IDs; 5) containment invariant lands 9fc4b4cf (supervisor off data path, restart policy, health aggregation); 6) gates.

GATES: ruff check+format; targeted pytest (tests/server, contract); scripts/benchmark_startup (boot fan-out is this design's hot path); no benchmark regression before merge.

PRECEDENT: design-record style = 4a1e62fa (domain consolidation design record). Expert review given to user 2026-10-27 (cell architecture / containment / events; two refinements: facts-not-requests + compose-existing-cards).
title: CELLS architecture: workspace as instantiable whole-app space + containment + typed event envelope (composes ecea49c8 + 8fe718f5 + 9fc4b4cf)

notes.text:
RE-TRIAGE (2026-10-28, investigated then parked by user decision — design recorded, no code written).

PREMISE SHIFT: the three-tier transport seam (card ad4f5ec2, landed main e888d5da6 AFTER this card was written) defused the headline scenario — without MAN_API_URL the shell now dispatches IN-PROCESS (local_api.py) and never HTTP, so "dev server without MAN_API_URL cross-calls :8000" cannot happen through _api_get/_api_post anymore.

Remaining cross-call surface (all verified in code):
1. `--remote` without MAN_API_URL: is_remote_mode() true via _FORCE_REMOTE, get_api_base() falls to hardcoded :8000 -> talks to whoever owns it.
2. api start Phase 1/2 (runtime.py): attaches to ANY healthy server on the default port and reports "connected (model)" — instance B silently joins instance A; Phase 3 spawns only when the port is free. No instance identity in /health.
3. Split-brain env vars: clients read MAN_API_URL (config.py), spawn side reads API_BASE (runtime.py:58) — MAN_API_URL=...:8001 + api start still spawns/attaches on 8000.
4. DEFAULT_API_BASE captured at import time (stale if env changes).

DESIGN DECIDED (user answers 2026-10-28):

description:
QUESTION (user, 2026-10-27): how do we KNOW SloNet's architecture is different from other models (Qwen/GPT-class)? Answer must be mechanical (green/red), not vibes.

FINDING — the primitive already exists (port-don't-rebuild): domain/infrastructure/_internal/arch_config.py = architecture-as-data (4 feature flags: norm/positional/activation/attention) + build_arch(config.json, weight_keys) auto-detection + GPT2/LLAMA/NATIVE weight maps. Tests exist for detection (test_arch_config.py, test_infrastructure_arch_config.py) but NOTHING fingerprints OUR native model vs references, and nothing pins the difference contracts.

HONEST DIFFERENTIATOR TABLE (read from slonet.py, 8273 lines):
- SAME family (by design, "drop-in replacement"): decoder-only, pre-norm, RoPE, RMSNorm, gated GLU FFN (w1/w3 product), GQA support, tied weights — the llama/Qwen recipe.
- DIFFERENT (provable): (1) substrate = pure NumPy from-scratch (own autograd Tensor, optimizers, KV cache; ZERO torch/transformers imports — verified 0 mentions); (2) native tensor naming (tok_emb/blocks.0.ff.w1 vs model.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj) via NATIVE_WEIGHT_MAP identity map; (3) soul metadata on every model (soul_name/lineage/soul_traits {warmth,creativity,curiosity,confidence} — "every model IS a soul"; no HF analog); (4) .slnc + quant sidecar serialization; (5) layer zoo beyond transformers (SloLSTM, SloConv2D, SloBatchNorm2D).

DELIVERABLE: packages/core-py/tests/test_slonet_arch_fingerprint.py — three pinned contracts:
1. SAME-family: native fingerprint (build_arch over a tiny SloTransformer's real state_dict keys + eps/rope from the instance) == llama/Qwen-family reference flags.
2. DISCRIMINANT: GPT-2 reference flags differ in all four; native weight-map resolve() differs from HF llama naming; transpose orientation contract (ours False vs GPT2 True).
3. DIFFERENCE contracts: AST import audit (no torch/transformers/tensorflow anywhere in slonet.py), layer-zoo classes exist, soul metadata present.
If a future change makes us silently MORE like HF (or breaks drop-in compatibility), this goes red.

GATES: ruff check/format + pytest packages/core-py/tests/test_slonet_arch_fingerprint.py + adjacent (test_arch_config, test_infrastructure_arch_config, test_slonet_wave_a).
title: SloNet arch fingerprint test: prove same-family recipe + real differences vs other models

description:
DEFECT (user review of 'state dict vs state graph', 2026-10-27): SloNet._rebuild_from_state_dict (slonet.py:4180) and its forward partner _forward_state_dict (:4302) only understand the LEGACY key family (blocks.{i}.norm1 / blocks.{i}.mlp.w1 — as pinned by the two hand-built legacy tests) and cannot consume the CURRENT native state_dict that SloTransformer.state_dict() actually produces (blocks.{i}.attn_norm / blocks.{i}.ff.w1).

LIVE-PROBED EVIDENCE (tiny SloTransformer 64 emb / 2 layer / 4 head / 2 kv, fed DIRECTly):
- Structure probes miss -> rebuild reports hidden=384 (fallback; truth 64), ff_dim=1536 (hidden*4; truth 192 = align_dim_ff(170)), n_heads=6 (384//64; truth 4). Only the block COUNT (2) is right — it comes from the keys, not the name probes.
- _forward_state_dict CRASHES: _sd_get('blocks.0.norm1.weight') cannot see native attn_norm -> weight=None -> _layernorm_state_dict does 'float * None' -> TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'float' and 'NoneType'. mlp.w1 lookup equally blind to ff.w1 (would AttributeError next).
- heads-from-shapes is UNDERDETERMINED for GQA (q_out=n_heads*head_dim admits many splits) — structure must come from metadata/keys, never be guessed from square-matrix shapes. _SoulTransformerBlockSoulLib is stateless bookkeeping (forward=identity, parameters=[]) so wrong dims corrupt metadata/optimizer surfaces, not the math; the MATH crashes as above.

REACHABILITY (honest): the file loader routes native keys to the correct SloTransformer path (is_transformer includes any(k.startswith('blocks.'))), so production .soul/.slnc loading is unaffected TODAY. The crash/misdimension fires on the DIRECT API — exactly what SloNet(state_dict-of-a-SloTransformer) composition, foreign dumps, and the existing direct-call tests use. Latent API defect, one-call fix.

FIX (surgical, slonet.py only — no format change, no loader change):
1. _rebuild_from_state_dict: hidden = metadata flat keys (n_embed/hidden_size) -> tok_emb.shape[1] (always present, IS hidden by definition) -> legacy norm probes; n_heads = metadata (n_head/num_attention_heads) -> existing q-probe unchanged for legacy; ff = metadata (intermediate_size) -> ff.w1 -> mlp.w1 -> w1 -> hidden*4.
2. _sd_get fallback chain gains native names: norm1<->attn_norm, norm2<->ff_norm, mlp.wN<->ff.wN (keeps all three legacy families working — they pin their names in tests).
3. _layernorm_state_dict(None) -> return input unchanged (currently a TypeError) — behavior change only where it used to crash.

TESTS (red-first): packages/core-py/tests/test_slonet_rebuild_native.py — (a) rebuild dims match the source SloTransformer's weights (hidden 64 / ff 192 / blocks 2), (b) metadata preference for heads (4, not shape-guess), (c) forward on a native state_dict serves (shape (1,N,vocab), finite, layernorm spy receives the real attn_norm/ff_norm arrays — never None), (d) legacy families keep passing via the existing wave_a + legacy suites.

GATES: ruff check/format + new file + family gate packages/core-py -k 'slonet or arch_config' (2183 baseline).
title: SloNet rebuild/forward blind to native key family: wrong dims (384/1536/6-head) + forward TypeError on native state_dict

description:
ARCHITECTURE (user ruling, 2026-10-28 — three-tier split, OpenAI-analog):
- binary = MODEL tier (engine + domain core). The shell is PART of it: sloughgpt shell already imports domain.shell in-process (DaitRuntime/ShellREPL/Kernel/VMRunner).
- API server = CLOUD tier: the ONLY HTTP tier (auth, sessions, SSE, rate control) — for web UI + remote API clients.
- web UI + remote/mobile API clients = CLIENTS of the cloud (http-client.ts single transport; endpoints = descriptor projections).

DEFECT: domain/shell/_internal/commands.py has 21 _api_post() + _api_delete() call sites — core->core calls routed over loopback HTTP — and cli.py `shell` calls ensure_server() (spawns a server just to make function calls). Same process = function call; different process = transport crossing (AGENTS.md boundary test). Boundary defect.

SCOPE (what MUST be affected): shell path only — in-process is the DEFAULT, ensure_server leaves the shell path, HTTP demoted to explicit REMOTE mode (MAN_API_URL set / --remote flag / pointed at another host: controlling a running daemon is real usage).
MUST NOT be affected: any web route; remote-client behavior; contracts.gen.ts / tool descriptors (endpoints stay projections — no contract churn); mobile (stays a web client); split of `serve --web` deployment bundling (separate future card).

MECHANISM (refinement 1): three consumers of ONE contract — web/remote via HTTP projection (unchanged), shell via in-process domain calls (new seam), CLI subcommands unchanged. Process-local singletons (server_state, download_manager, cancel_manager...) MOVE INTO domain/ (port, don't rebuild) so router and shell each own one copy in their own process; routers stay thin projections. Trust model: in-process CLI = same-user local, no auth — deliberate.

TEST (red-first): shell server-dependent commands run with NO server + ensure_server blocked; remote-mode test proves HTTP still engages when explicitly targeted.
GATES: shell suite + ruff check/format + family gate packages/core-py -k 'slonet or arch_config' baseline; shell startup latency benchmark (no server spawn = improvement).
ALSO (doc): tier table + one-paragraph rule into docs/PRODUCT_ENGINEERING.md architecture section — no behavior change.
title: Shell binary runs core in-process: API server is web/client-only (three-tier: binary=model / server=cloud / web+clients=clients)

description:
Found during version-tracking audit (card f8d4c968): FeatureFlags.load_config() has zero production callers — grep across apps/, domain/, scripts/ shows only tests. config/feature_flags.json is therefore dead config; flag statuses come from code defaults + SLO_FF_* env vars only. Consequence: hf_finetune reads enabled in config but disabled in code, and nobody can tell because the file is never read. DECISION NEEDED before wiring: enabling load_config at boot would flip hf_finetune to enabled (only divergent flag of 24). Either wire load_config into startup.py with a review of that divergence, or retire the config file. The new flag_history.jsonl ledger records divergence on first load.

RESOLVED 2026-10-31 (lane feat/wire-flag-load-config, user ruling: WIRE load_config at boot). config/feature_flags.json was DEAD — declared intent but nothing called load_config(), so the in-memory registry kept code defaults and is_enabled('hf_finetune') read DISABLED.

Change (apps/api/server/main.py lifespan): guarded FeatureFlags.load_config() at the TOP of lifespan, BEFORE StartupOrchestrator.run() — orchestration phases (startup.py:633,1502) and provider setup (setup.py:114) call is_enabled, so hydration must precede them. Wrapped in try/except so a malformed/missing config logs a warning and boot proceeds on defaults (never blocks boot).

Scope verified minimal: load_config flips exactly ONE flag — hf_finetune disabled->enabled. The other 23 config flags already match their registered defaults; 2 registered flags are absent from config (keep default). Behaviorally INERT today: no non-test code calls is_enabled('hf_finetune') (the only consumer, training/builds.py, scans a directory, not the flag) — the flip just makes the flag truthful to the declared config. The append-only ledger dedupes via _last_recorded_statuses, so first boot records one status entry and restarts never spam.

Test (tests/core-py/test_feature_flags.py, NEW test_real_config_enables_hf_finetune): pins the real config/feature_flags.json declares hf_finetune enabled AND load_config applies it (DISABLED->ENABLED, is_enabled False->True). Reads real config content, applies via tmp_path so the ledger writes to tmp (fixture) not the repo config/ dir. Existing test_known_flags_default_status (pins DISABLED) stays green — it asserts the registration default and pytest never runs lifespan.

Evidence: tests/core-py/test_feature_flags.py 75/75 passed; ruff clean on main.py + test file; main.py py_compile ok; grep confirms zero non-test is_enabled(hf_finetune) consumers.
title: feature_flags.json is never loaded at boot (config inert)

description: Found 2026-10-29 on PR #239 (run 40815499806, head 02b489cc), rerun green. Mechanism: packages/core-py/tests/test_quantization_benchmark_e2e.py::TestBaseline::test_baseline_cli_json_block runs scripts/benchmark_quantization.py --quick twice (run 1 writes baseline, run 2 compares) and asserts regressions == []. The 7 quick sub-tests include timing-gated speed checks (_speed_gate: tiny scale = geomean >= 0.3 sanity band, documented as machine-state dependent — float32 numpy path swings ~4x with CPU boost/BLAS state). On a loaded runner a speed sub-test flips pass<->fail between the two back-to-back runs, so the aggregate passed count differs (baseline 6 vs current 5) and _compare_baselines gates passed as never-drop -> AssertionError. Proven NOT a code regression: CI/CD was green at c100addd on the SAME core-py/quantization code (git diff c100addd..02b489cce -- packages/core-py domain apps/api = empty), failed only at 02b489cc; gh run rerun --failed then passed. Class: environmental flake, carded not fixed in-PR (same precedent as the root-suite environmental failures). Fix direction: either make tiny-scale speed gates purely informational so they cannot flip the aggregate passed count (the docstring already says informational at tiny scale — the gate still flips it), or exclude speed-derived sub-test results from the passed gate for tiny runs while keeping quality/compression sub-tests gated; alternative is a ±1 tolerance on passed in baseline compare, but that weakens a real gate — prefer the first two. Evidence: gh run view 40815499806 --log-failed; note tests/test_quantization_benchmark_e2e.py lives in packages/core-py/tests/ (root tests/ does not contain it).

description:
Found 2026-10-30 on PR #252 (CI/CD run 41023825495, job 123957125782, head 8aa351602). The lowercase lint job (distinct from the web Lint job, which passed) FAILED at 4m24s — but never reached any repo code.

Mechanism: the CI/CD workflow lint job does pip install ruff==0.16.8 mypy. The GitHub Actions runner could not resolve pypi.org: 5x NameResolutionError("HTTPSConnection(host='pypi.org', port=443): Failed to resolve 'pypi.org' ([Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution)") -> ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement ruff==0.16.8 (from versions: none) -> ERROR: No matching distribution found for ruff==0.16.8 -> exit code 1. This is pure CI-runner network egress/DNS flakiness during the pip step, NOT a lint violation in the diff (ruff was never installed, so no file was linted).

Proven environmental, not code: (a) the sibling web Lint job (run 41023825539) passed 34s on the SAME head; (b) local ruff on every touched file (tests/skip_gate_identity.py, tests/test_skip_gate_identity.py, tests/test_integration.py, tests/test_header_screenshots.py, scripts/benchmark_results.py) is clean; (c) the failure text is a DNS/name-resolution error, not a rule violation.

Class: environmental flake, carded not fixed in-PR (same precedent as card 20261029_074304 and the root-suite environmental failures). The run was still in_progress (test-core-py pending) so gh could not rerun-failed-jobs until completion; once complete, rerun the failed job — expected green.

Fix direction (infra, not this lane): the lint job depends on live pypi.org egress with no cache/retry pin; either (1) rely on the pip cache action already present so a cache hit avoids the index entirely, or (2) add a retry/backoff around the pip install step, or (3) pre-install ruff in the runner image / use a requirements lock with a vendored wheel so a DNS blip cannot redden the gate. description:
Diagnosis: audit of the 8 agent-loop tool implementations in domain/agents/_internal/agents.py found real correctness bugs (same class as the file_search --max-count=0 zero-results bug, already fixed on main):

1. _execute_subprocess uses bare python3 from PATH, not sys.executable — code runs outside the sloughgpt env (missing deps/wrong interpreter). asyncio.wait_for timeout cancels communicate() but never kills the child — orphaned processes survive timeouts.
2. _search_web: no follow_redirects (DDG POST 302s to empty), no raise_for_status (403 bot pages => silent success:0), results carry no url (citations impossible).
3. file_read / file_search(path) / data_analysis / image_analysis accept arbitrary model-supplied paths with zero restriction (SecurityConfig.allowed_directories exists but is never read; ~/.ssh/.env readable). Sensitive-dir + .env blocklist, honor allowlist when configured.
4. data_analysis: jsonl truncated at 500KB mid-line => whole tool errors; no truncation flag on CSV/JSON counts (silent wrong totals).
5. knowledge fallback: full-substring query match => near-zero recall, silent empty.
6. image_analysis: ImportError/vision errors return success:True (masks failure).
7. test_real_grep asserts only isinstance(list) — would never catch a zero-results bug.

Plan: branch fix/agent-tools-correctness; fixes + tests in tests/core-py/test_agent_core.py; gates = ruff check/format + 61+ core-py agent tests + server agent router tests; merge to main when green; AGENT_SYNC entry; benchmark n/a (tool plumbing, not model perf).

description: Step 4 of the approved always-record plan (user ruling 2026-10-31: 'always structure our data so we don't lose it / can train on it'). The always-record store landed (5516b4835): every benchmark record now lands in ONE checkout-independent series at ~/.local/share/sloughgpt/benchmark_results (SLO_BENCH_DATA_DIR env override), stamped source: local|ci, with migrate --from to union old per-checkout stores. 6 records already migrated (5 inference + 1 startup); fresh decode run 19.27 tok/s r2=0.9999. PROBLEM this card solves: Site Doctor's inference triage currently reads a SINGLE snapshot metric (or no metric) — it cannot tell 'this run is slow' from 'this run is slow RELATIVE TO TREND under comparable load'. A raw tok/s number is meaningless without the load context (same script measured 9.8 -> 19.27 tok/s across runs as load/turbo changed). BUILD: a reader over the record series that the Site Doctor inference check calls — (a) load the series for a given script/benchmark id, (b) compute trend (linear fit / moving median over last N runs) + spread (sigma), (c) compare the current run's value against trend: within k*sigma = healthy, below = regression candidate (report slope), (d) emit a compact summary (current, trend arrow, sigma band, n runs, source mix local|ci) — NOT a raw dump (summarize-don't-dump rule). STATISTICAL trend/sigma-gating first, NOT gradient training — the 'train on it' ruling's first consumer is regression gating: catch inference-speed/quality drift across runs automatically rather than a human eyeballing one number. Consumer = Site Doctor's inference triage path (the 'site doctor' the user ruled we are building). Integrate as a reader module the doctor calls; do NOT build a new page (page rule: no journey for it — operator surface stays inline). GATES: unit tests for trend/sigma math on synthetic series (monotonic, flat, noisy, single-run edge case = too-few-samples -> 'insufficient history' not a false alarm), ruff, change-scoped run. description:
SYMPTOM: server-side inference measured ~0.36 tok/s over HTTP while the in-process decode benchmark measured 17.0 tok/s (47x gap). Root cause is NOT the KV cache (kv_quant = 1.5% of decode) and NOT a leak (210 GETs across 17 endpoints + 9 POSTs left RSS flat at 1.98 GB, exactly 1 model load, 21 threads).

ROOT CAUSE: the numpy fallback in domain/training/_internal/slonet_kernels.py fused_attention_multi (lines 788-797; the numba call is line 786) materializes ~4 concurrent (H, seq, seq) float32 temporaries: scores, scores+causal, exp(...), attn/sum. With H=16 and max_seq_len=32768 (from Qwen max_position_embeddings):
  seq 4096 -> 4.0 GB, seq 8192 -> 16.0 GB, seq 16384 -> 64.0 GB
total_len = min(prompt_len + max_new, 32768) therefore imposes NO practical cap. Observed server anon-rss of 20.5-21.4 GB matches seq~8192 plus 2 GB of weights.

EVIDENCE the server took the numpy fallback rather than numba: thread dumps from the OOM-killed pid 1600 show slonet_kernels.py lines 792/794/795 inside fused_attention_multi, reached from slonet.py:7331 generate_numpy_stream. Line 786 (the numba call) was never the sampled line. numba works fine in a standalone shell (_nb_fused_attention_multi: True) but _ensure_fused() fails SILENTLY inside the server -- that gap is unexplained and is the highest-value fix: the numba path writes only out (seq,H,E_head) = 32 MB and never materializes (H,seq,seq) at all.

THE FIX ORDER (user-approved 2026-11-01):
1. Surface why _ensure_fused() fails inside the server so the numba path runs. This removes the quadratic allocation outright. Numba is present in the env (numba 0.67.0, llvmlite 0.49.0, numpy 2.5.3).
2. Blockwise-chunk the numpy fallback (defense in depth, not the primary lever). Prefill memory must be O(seq), not O(seq^2). Learn the blockwise technique from GGUF/llama.cpp but DO NOT add either as a dependency.
3. Clamp prefill total_len to a sane CPU limit. Scope correction: cap PREFILL only. Generation already streams fine and must NOT be affected.
4. Fix the misleading EMERGENCY message. apps/api/server/routers/inference.py:254 prints a freshly re-read psutil percent, so it reported 56% while the classification that blocked the request was >=95%. It must print the reading that TRIGGERED classification. Proven in journal: 10:49:10 CRI memory_pressure EMERGENCY 96.1% (19074 MB RSS), then 10:50:19 ERR chat "System memory at 56%", then 10:51:52 kernel OOM-killed pid 1600.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: no new training loops -- SloughGPTTrainer / SloChatTrainer adapters only. Work in worktree .wt-prefill on branch fix/prefill-attention-oom (created off main e59d03b19). The main working tree is occupied by another session (fix/audit-a11y-design-tokens, 2001 staged files) -- do NOT touch it. NOTE: slonet_kernels.py is currently STAGED-MODIFIED by that other session (a serial rewrite of both attention kernels adding a GQA reps parameter); coordinate before merging so their work is not clobbered.

VERIFY: (a) the canonical chat request "Count 1 to 10, one per line. Just numbers." returns 1..10 clean with zero leak markers (<|, endoftext, 三明治, <|im_start|>, User:, Assistant:) and does not overrun past 10; (b) POST /inference/generate "count 1 to 5" -> 1..5; (c) a long-prompt soak (>=8k tokens) with RSS watched via /proc must stay under ~4 GB; (d) scripts/benchmark_latency.py does not regress; (e) the chat and tools regression suites are green via scripts/run_affected.sh.
title: fix(inference): prefill attention numpy fallback allocates O(seq^2) -- the real cause of 1 tok/s (kernel OOM)

description:
FINDING: the recurring server SIGSEGV is NOT in model code. It is in the periodic stack dumper.

EVIDENCE -- two cores, byte-identical fault site, 16 hours apart:
  Oct 31 19:22 pid 978926 thread 978928  RIP python3.12 + 0x1a3c7b
  Nov 01 11:17 pid 68187  thread 68189   RIP python3.12 + 0x1a3c7b
addr2line + objdump resolve 0x1a3c7b to dump_traceback+0xbc in CPython traceback.c:1259. The disassembly decodes as:
  1a3c76  call   _Py_write_noraise
  1a3c7b  mov    0x70(%r14),%rax      <- SIGSEGV: stale pointer in %r14
  1a3c84  mov    0x8(%rax),%rax       ob_type
  1a3c88  testb  $0x10,0xab(%rax)     Py_TPFLAGS_UNICODE_SUBCLASS  (PyUnicode_Check)
  1a3ca6  call   _Py_DumpASCII
%r14 is a PyCodeObject*, 0x70(%r14) is co_filename, and it then runs PyUnicode_Check on the result. Frame #1 (PyCode_Type) is a .data address, i.e. a garbage unwind, so only RIP is trustworthy.

WHICH KERNEL WAS LIVE at each crash -- this is what rules the kernels out as the direct cause:
  Oct 31 -> numba cache file _fused_attention_multi-558 (Oct 25/29) = the OLD parallel=True + prange(H*seq_len) version
  Nov 01 -> numba cache file _fused_attention_multi-595 (Nov 1 10:42) = the NEW serial rewrite
Both crashed identically. Neither the prange version nor the serial rewrite is the cause; what they share is nogil=True (landed 54c9d300c, Oct 6), which releases the GIL while the kernel runs. Combined with SLO_DUMP_STACKS=1 in the systemd unit (live unit mtime Oct 11), which calls faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(30, repeat=True) and walks EVERY thread's frame chain every 30 s -- precisely the code that trips over a thread parked inside a nogil call.

This also re-explains the red herrings: the dumper kept catching innocent frames (quantization.py summary(), watchdog.py, model_health.py, process_guard.py) because it samples everything. It was the tripwire, not the culprit. Note SLO_DUMP_STACKS is documented in main.py as temporary "drill instrumentation".

USER RULING (2026-11-01): keep the dumper, but stop the cross-thread C walk.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE -- the literal request is not expressible in the stdlib API. faulthandler.dump_traceback_later() has NO all_threads parameter; it always walks every thread. The only way to dump "current thread only" is faulthandler.dump_traceback(all_threads=False), but called from the timer thread that would dump the timer thread's own idle stack every tick -- zero diagnostic value for hang diagnosis, which is the entire point of the tool.

The implementation that honours the ruling's intent (keep a live multi-thread dumper) while removing the exact crashing instruction is to walk the threads in PYTHON via sys._current_frames(), which returns frame objects the caller HOLDS STRONG REFERENCES to. That removes faulthandler's raw C-level co_filename deref -- the precise instruction at 0x1a3c7b -- while still showing every thread.

This doubles as a TEST OF THE HYPOTHESIS: if SIGSEGV persists after the switch, that proves genuine heap corruption in the kernels rather than a faulthandler walk defect, and points the investigation straight back at card for the prefill attention work.

OWNED PATH: apps/api/server/main.py (_install_stack_dump_timer at line 234, _cancel_stack_dump_timer at line 259). Preserve the SLO_DUMP_STACKS / SLO_DUMP_STACKS_INTERVAL env contract and the stderr destination; systemd journal captures stderr. Stale tests/server/test_stack_dump_timer.cpython-312-pytest-9.1.1.pyc exists with no .py source -- do not resurrect it, just do not leave a new .pyc.

VERIFY: with SLO_DUMP_STACKS=1 and SLO_DUMP_STACKS_INTERVAL=2 the server logs a dump every 2 s showing multiple real threads (the uvicorn event loop, the pool, watchdog) not just the dumper; the dump output still reaches journalctl --user -u slough-api; and no SIGSEGV occurs across a soak with concurrent inference requests.

CLOSED 2026-11-03: fixed by 392fa637a (GIL-safe stack-dump thread, sys._current_frames walk) — confirmed ancestor of main; done-card 20261102_020229 tracks the verification.
title: fix(server): periodic stack dumper SIGSEGVs at dump_traceback+0xbc walking other threads' frames

description:

description: Audit finding (card 20261101_104216, finding 3): /consciousness/dashboard renders BLANK — journey blocker. Root cause: consciousnessController.getQualia() is typed Promise<Record<string,number>> but the backend returns {current:{valence...},narrative,history_count} (apiGet unwraps envelope.data at apps/lib/request.ts:255). useConsciousnessDashboard stores the whole object as currentQualia; CurrentStateFold (components/DashboardFolds.tsx:94) calls (v as number).toFixed(2) on the nested 'current' object -> TypeError crash-loop on every live refresh -> blank page. PRE-EXISTING: identical line in pre-decomposition page.tsx:166 (decompose refactor moved it verbatim). Test mock (page.test.tsx:86) replicated the wrong flat shape so tests stayed green. FIX: (1) controller getQualia return type -> envelope shape; (2) hook: setCurrentQualia(value.current ?? {}); (3) test mock -> real backend shape + assert qualia bars render; (4) fold: Number.isFinite guard so a future shape drift degrades to bars-skipped, never a blank page. Consumer check: getQualia() used only by this hook. Gates: tsc, eslint, vitest dashboard closure, then RE-SCREENSHOT to prove the page renders (audit methodology). benchmark n/a (bugfix).
title: Fix consciousness dashboard blank render — getQualia envelope stored as flat map crashes CurrentStateFold

description: Supersedes parked card 63116e83 (gone from board). ADAPTERS ARE THE NOUN: per-training-task artifacts (text-pretrain, tts-espeak, image-caption, chat-sft), never per-source. Sources = 4 closed config kinds (local/http/kaggle/shell operator-tier only); config names components, never contains them; new source = one YAML line, zero rebuild. TRAINER SEAM: BatchArray protocol (re-iterable, sized, shufflable — map-style Dataset contract, NOT a one-shot iterator: epochs+shuffle require collection semantics); every adapter implements it; adapters never import the loop; exactly ONE seam on SloughGPTTrainer. COMPOSITION GATE: AUTOMATIC, not on-demand — three layers: (a) fail-fast at registry boot (broken adapter never registers), (b) static parametrized pytest over the whole registry asserting declared in/out contracts compose (test_command_parity.py shape), (c) one dynamic synthetic smoke: tiny fixture batch through the real AML pipeline (dedup -> quality -> snapshot -> BatchArray) proving runtime shape. AML cruncher pipeline is the canonical flow passing through the gate (dogfood). 100% registry coverage from day one, no grandfather baseline; rides affected-closure loop AND every full-CI run (seam gate, Test Rule clause 4); never requires real credentials/datasets — synthetic only; ONE parametrized gate, not per-adapter tests. SCOPE: weights training only (knowledge store out per parked ruling); espeak_pairs grandfathered until BatchArray byte-parity; spine builds on the FIRST real training task, not before; sources get their 4 kinds at that same trigger; modality payloads live inside the batch, not the contract. AML import->clean->snapshot design rides here.
title: Training adapters: standing design ruling (adapters are the noun; BatchArray seam; automatic composition gate via AML)

description:
Two bound sets now govern meta-weight output at two layers, and the lower one is generation-UNSAFE.

(1) DOMAIN — _SAFE_BAND in domain/feedback/_internal/meta_weights.py get_adjustment() (commit 472565281): tight neutral+/-band window. temp (0.3,1.1), rep (1.0,1.25), top_p (0.6,1.0), top_k (10,120). Fixes the /chat infinite-repetition loop at the source.

(2) TRANSPORT — _META_WEIGHT_BOUNDS in apps/api/server/routers/inference.py _apply_meta_weights() (commit 3384d08dd, card 1e13f836): clamps to GenerateRequest FIELD bounds, drift-gated by tests/test_meta_weights_clamp.py. temp (0,2), rep (0.5,2), top_p (0,1), top_k (0,500).

THE PROBLEM: (2) is schema-valid but generation-unsafe. repetition_penalty 0.5 passes pydantic and ACTIVELY REWARDS REPEATING TOKENS — it is the loop itself. The live /chat bug was temp 1.5 / top_k 5 / rep 0.80; with bounds (2) alone, a saturated accumulator still lands on rep 0.5. (1) keeps the real path out of reach, so the hazard is latent, not live — but any bypass of get_adjustment() (mock, refactor, alternate manager) restores it.

ALSO DUPLICATED CONCERN: (2)'s comment claims the bounds mirror GenerateRequest, but the schema bounds and the generation-safe bounds are different facts written twice at one seam. Decide ONE authority:
  a) raise _META_WEIGHT_BOUNDS rep floor 0.5 -> 1.0 and tighten temp/upper, then make (1) the only other clamp; or
  b) keep (2) purely as schema validation, rename to say so, and let (1) own generation safety — but then assert      the domain band is applied on every path (incl. cached nudges, which bypass get_adjustment()).

DECIDED 2026-11-01: ship the domain band only (472565281) and card this, to avoid rewriting another contributor's landed contract (test_meta_weights_clamp.py asserts rep 0.2 -> 0.5) in the same change. NOTE the nudge cache: _META_WEIGHT_CACHE stores nudges for 5s, and a cached nudge bypasses get_adjustment() entirely, so the band does NOT protect a cache hit if the nudge was computed pre-band or by an unbanded path.

Acceptance: one documented authority for generation-safe bounds; test_meta_weights_clamp.py updated to the chosen semantics; a test proving the band is applied on the cache-hit path too.

notes.text: LANDED-ELSEWHERE: commit 472565281 ('_SAFE_BAND' in meta_weights.py) is NOT an ancestor of main — it never landed (git merge-base --is-ancestor = NO; grep _SAFE_BAND on main = 0 hits). 67364e35d supersedes its intent with a different mechanism: per-field integration CAPS on the stored boosts (write + read, so existing saturated rows repair without a migration) plus a repetition_penalty floor of 1.0 in get_adjustment(). Live 'default' row now reads boosts 0.3 / -0.15 / -12 instead of 9.26 / -9.26 / -450, and the implicit /inference/generate request lands at temp 1.0 / top_p 1.0 / top_k 28 / rep 1.0. REMAINING WORK ON THIS CARD: (1) _META_WEIGHT_BOUNDS in apps/api/server/routers/inference.py still clamps repetition_penalty to a floor of 0.5 — schema-valid but generation-unsafe, so any path bypassing get_adjustment() (mock, refactor, alternate manager) restores the reward-repetition loop; decide one authority (recommended: keep that dict as SCHEMA validation only, rename/document it as such, and let get_adjustment() own generation safety, then assert merged-on-nudge == adj and that GenerateRequest defaults == MetaWeights() neutral so the nudge delta cannot silently offset); (2) update tests/test_meta_weights_clamp.py to the chosen semantics; (3) add the cache-hit test — _META_WEIGHT_CACHE stores nudges for 5s and a hit skips get_adjustment(), so prove a cached nudge still yields a safe merged value.

description: Real pre-existing bug flagged during the vm page decomposition (AGENT_SYNC 20261101_052821, 'follow-up candidate'): apps/web/app/(app)/vm/useVmPage.ts handleRun reads keyboardInput inside the callback but its useCallback deps are [source, maxSteps, role, debug] — keyboardInput missing. Consequence: type into the Keyboard input field, press Run without touching anything else -> vmController.run receives the STALE keyboardInput from when the callback was last rebuilt (typically undefined/empty), so guest programs reading INT 0x80 keyboard input silently get old/empty input. The eslint react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warning (pre-existing, recorded through the decomposition) points at exactly this. FIX: add keyboardInput to the deps array (behavior: callback rebuilds on each keystroke — cheap, it already does for source). TDD: colocated page.test.tsx test typing into the keyboard input then running asserts run() receives the typed value; expect RED pre-fix (stale/undefined) -> GREEN post-fix. Gates: tsc, eslint (warning count should DROP by 1), vitest vm closure, audit greps. benchmark n/a (bugfix). SOP: branch fix/vm-keyboard-input-stale-closure from origin/main, push HEAD:main with AGENT_SYNC entry, card done with evidence.
title: Fix VM console stale keyboard input on Run — handleRun omits keyboardInput from useCallback deps

description: Gap found while verifying the 'we already have resumability' claim (user was right — everything below EXISTS): JobStore persists jobs across restarts; TrainingRuntime.shutdown gives trainers a cancel signal to save a final checkpoint; POST /recovery/recover/{job_id} resumes from the last checkpoint (recorded path authoritative, corrupt mid-write skipped, creates recovery_<id> job); GET /recovery/recoverable + StatusBar recovery panel expose it; periodic checkpoints every 500 steps bound hard-kill loss. MISSING: nothing auto-resumes on boot — restore() marks stale running rows interrupted and seeds the panel; a human clicks Recover. PRODUCT CALL NEEDED before building: (a) keep manual (safe: an expensive run restarts only when someone asks — no surprise GPU burn after an infra reboot, no resume storms when many jobs were interrupted), or (b) auto-resume on boot (hands-off continuity: an infra crash becomes a pause; needs a policy anyway — max concurrent resumes, skip if checkpoint missing/corrupt, maybe only jobs explicitly flagged auto_resume in their config). If (b): one startup hook iterating store.recoverable() through the existing recovery path + config flag + tests; endpoints/panel stay as-is. Precedent: the model-inference watchdog in main.py deliberately chose LOG-ONLY ('model reload from a watchdog thread is dangerous') — same class of decision, same posture likely applies.
title: Decide: boot-time auto-resume of interrupted training jobs (manual Recover is the status quo)

description:
apps/api/server/main.py _install_stack_dump_timer (line ~234) / _cancel_stack_dump_timer (~259). faulthandler.dump_traceback_later periodic dumper was root-caused as the SIGSEGV trigger. User ruling at time: keep the dumper, dump CURRENT THREAD only — then shelved after it was shown dump_traceback_later has no all_threads parameter, and a current-thread-only dump from the timer thread would just print the timer's own useless stack. Real options to record: (a) Python-level fix: schedule the dumper on a timer but have it walk sys._current_frames() and write each thread's traceback via faulthandler.dump_traceback(file) — per-thread dumps without faulthandler's C-level all-threads walk, (b) drop the periodic timer entirely and dump only synchronously from signal handlers / on-watchdog, (c) keep as-is if a later repro disproves the causality. Evidence + repro steps from the original diagnosis session should be re-checked before choosing (this was shelved, not verified to root). DoD: reproduce or disprove, land the chosen mechanism with a test, remove the shelved state.

CLOSED 2026-11-03: superseded — option (a) implemented in 392fa637a (GIL-safe thread + sys._current_frames), ancestor of main; done-card 20261102_020229 cites it.
title: SIGSEGV server crash: faulthandler periodic dumper suspected — fix shelved, pick up (sys._current_frames walk vs drop timer)

description:
FINDING (2026-11-02, observed while verifying card 20261101_110410 on the live server :8000): the canonical prompt "Count 1 to 10, one per line. Just numbers." streams 1..10 clean (zero leak markers) and then REPEATS the block: 1..10 x3 within max_tokens=64. POST /inference/generate {"prompt":"count 1 to 5","max_tokens":48} returns 1..5 x5, and at max_tokens=256 returns the same block ~9 times.

NOT an overrun past 10 (never emits 11+) and NOT a leak (no <|, endoftext, 三明治, <|im_start|>, User:, Assistant:). The model completes the task correctly and then never stops — so the defect is at the stop/sampling seam, not in the weights.

INVESTIGATE (in order):
1. Is the generation config actually applying an EOS/stop set? Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct uses <|im_end|> (token 151645); if the sampler never checks it, no prompt can terminate early. Check the generate loop stop predicate and whether max_tokens is the ONLY exit.
2. Repetition penalty / no_repeat_ngram present in the config surface but unwired (or wired to 1.0)?
3. Chat template: is the prompt rendered with the instruct template (im_start/im_end) or raw? A raw prompt explains weak instruction-following but not non-termination.

SCOPE: sampling/stop seam only. Do NOT retrain. Do NOT touch model weights. Fix the max_tokens default too if it is the only exit.

VERIFY: canonical count-1-to-10 request ends after 10 with no repeated block; generate count 1 to 5 -> exactly 1..5; no leak markers; decode throughput not regressed (scripts/benchmark_latency.py).

notes.text: DONE (67364e35d + rehash decd93464). Root cause is the feedback meta-weight integrator, not the stop predicate. See commit message for full evidence: live row 473 up/10 down -> boosts 9.26 / -9.26 / -450 -> clamped temp 1.5 / top_k 5 / rep 0.8; a repetition penalty < 1 rewards already-emitted tokens, so the answer completes then replays and never emits <|im_end|>. Fix: bounded integrator (write+read caps), rep floor 1.0, deterministic fallback embedding, and `eos_token_id or 0` removal (token 0 = '!'). Verified live: pre-fix 96 tokens of repeated 1..10 (3/3); post-fix band yields 29 tokens, exactly 1..10 (3/3). 367 passed, domain rehash --check clean, ruff clean. NOTE: :8000 still runs pre-fix code; restart to pick it up.

title: fix(inference): chat/generate repeats the completed block instead of stopping

description:
SCOPED OUT of card 20261101_110410 item 3 (2026-11-02), deliberately, not silently.

WHY IT CHANGED SHAPE: item 3 was originally "clamp prefill total_len to a sane CPU limit" as OOM defence. The OOM is already gone — the numpy fallback is chunked over the query axis under SLO_PREFILL_FALLBACK_BUDGET_MB (a6c8f3b31, proven by tests/core-py/test_prefill_fallback.py), so prefill memory is O(seq), not O(seq^2). What remains is LATENCY, not safety: an 8k-token prefill is ~a minute of CPU inside a 120 s request timeout.

WHY THAT IS NOT A DRIVE-BY FIX: a token clamp means silently truncating the user prompt. Which end gets dropped (head for recency, tail for instructions), and whether truncation is announced, is a context-window product decision (docs/UX_FLOWS.md owns it) — not a kernel flag.

INVESTIGATE: measure prefill wall-clock vs prompt length on this box (seq 1k/2k/4k/8k, H=16, E_head=64); find where the 120 s timeout actually bites; then propose truncation semantics with the numbers attached.

SCOPE: prefill path only. Generation already streams fine and must NOT be affected (card 20261101_110410 scope correction).
title: perf(inference): prefill latency policy — cap CPU prefill work (scoped out of card 20261101_110410)

description:
LANDED on main (2026-11-02), recorded here because the originating cards lived only in the stale repo-local .kanban and never reached the canonical board.

WHY THIS CARD EXISTS: feat/provenance-lineage is 29 ahead / 680 behind origin/main. Port-don't-rebuild was applied file by file; these three commits proved ABSENT from main (grep prewarm_accelerator = 0 hits, session_id in routers/llm_v1.py = 0 hits, get_accelerator() still calling _detect_best_backend() inline), so they were cherry-picked rather than rebuilt.

WHAT LANDED (main, in order):
- d391ef04 fix(gpu): bounded, probe-once accelerator detection. The 2026-10-29 05:06 incident: the lazy cupy first-import hung natively UNDER a live /health request, poisoned the import lock, and because the backend cache only filled AFTER detection returned, every concurrent get_accelerator() caller re-entered detection and piled onto it — :8000 served nothing for 4+ minutes. Now one daemon probe per reset epoch, callers bounded by SLO_ACCEL_PROBE_TIMEOUT (default 5s) then CPU fallback + latch, late result supersedes (generation-guarded), reset bumps the generation to discard in-flight probes, and _CUDABackend.is_available() does a ctypes driver check BEFORE importing cupy.
- 4ef278cf fix(startup): prewarm kick moved to the executed staged_loader path. It had been in _phase_config — a hook with no runner on that line (proved by boot logs producing no probe) — so the first import still happened under live traffic.
- 3dbcac51 perf(api): /v1 chat/completions accepts session_id. ChatBody had no field and pydantic ignores extras, so external multi-turn clients had the key SILENTLY DISCARDED while SessionKVManager (LRU+TTL) sat unused below the seam and the whole prefix re-prefilled per request. Field + one injection point (stream inherits it) + CHAT_SPEC param, so the descriptor stays the contract source of truth.
- bbcfafba fix(gpu): reset_accelerator() never rebound _PROBE_DONE — MY BUG FOUND IN THE PORTED CODE, not in the fork. The rebind was written without _PROBE_DONE in the global statement, so it created a function-local and the module kept the previous epoch's already-SET event. Every post-reset get_accelerator() then saw wait() return instantly with _BACKEND still None and latched the CPU fallback — CUDA silently dropped for the process life. Measured: epoch 1 cuda 0.33s, epoch 2 cpu 0.0014s before; cuda 0.33/0.03/0.03 after. The imported suite was green because test_reset_allows_fresh_reprobe counts probe CALLS, not which backend was SERVED; the new test uses a _Sentinel(_CPUBackend) subclass plus a 0.05s probe because a trivial fake detector won the race against the stale event and hid the bug.

GATES (re-run, not trusted from commit messages): 209 passed across gpu-probe + /v1 router + prefill fallback + memory pressure + config + config router + process-guard default + startup preload + startup routers; tests/contract 43 passed; apps/api/server/tests/test_ts_contracts.py 6 passed (so the fork's regenerated contracts.gen.ts is byte-correct against main's generator); gen_router_manifest.py --check up to date (55 modules); ruff check + format clean.

NOT PORTED, deliberately: the selfgen block in train_pipeline.py (main has it; the fork copy is a merge artifact that DUPLICATES it) and apps/web/app/(app)/vm/page.tsx (+1631 lines = the pre-decomposition monolith). UI-only cosmetic diffs (globals.css gradients, navigation/redirects, package.json) left unported — no journey behind them.

SIDE EFFECTS: SLO_AUTH_REQUIRED and SLO_CORS_ORIGINS joined _SKIP_ENV_KEYS (both are read via os.environ on main and warned "Unknown config key" at boot). The fork's comment justifying them by a "fail-closed default" was NOT imported — main has default "false"; whether that default should flip remains the separate decision in card fcc6ebfe8.

── VERIFIED LIVE 2026-11-02 (added after the fact by the session that landed it) ──

RESTART: systemctl --user restart slough-api (the declarative path; the unit is byte-identical to scripts/systemd/slough-api.service). New MainPID 267247. Boot journal: probe complete 02:14:07 INSIDE "Stage CRITICAL", "Application startup complete" 02:14:18 — the probe now finishes 11s before anything can call into it. /health 200.

SESSION REUSE — IT WORKS, measured (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on :8000, 482-token prompt, temperature=0):
  turn 1 (cold), session=ext-A ......... 16.48s
  turn 2 EXTENDS turn 1, same session ... 1.96s   <- 17.4s saved by the resume
  turn 2 same messages, COLD session ... 19.38s
That is SloTransformer._resolve_kv_state resuming at start=482 instead of re-prefilling.

CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER READING OF THIS SAME VERIFICATION: `usage.prompt_tokens` is NOT evidence. routers/llm_v1.py:~332 computes it by estimating the request messages, so a warm turn reports the full 482 regardless. An initial probe replayed the SAME prompt and saw ~16s every time — that is NOT a broken cache: an identical prompt is an explicit degenerate case (`if 0 < s < prompt_len` with s == prompt_len -> start = 0), pinned by tests/core-py/test_slonet_kv_cache.py::test_resolve_identical_prompt_falls_back. Resume only fires when the new prompt EXTENDS the cached prefix, which is what session_id is for. The cost of that degenerate case is now card 20261102_012822_perfinference-a-repeated-identical-prompt-re-prefills-from-s.

REMAINING GAP (carded, not fixed): SloNetServer.generate() drops session_id on the ProcessGuard branch, so a DIRECT provider.chat() with a live guard silently loses reuse. /v1 is unaffected because ProviderRouter.chat delegates to chat_stream -> generate_stream -> pump, which honours it — proven by GET /models/process-guard reporting requests_served == 1 (boot warmup only) across 8 /v1 requests. Card 20261102_012822_fixguard-slonetservergenerate-drops-session-id-on-the-proces.

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 while verifying the /v1 session_id KV reuse that landed in bbcfafba1/3dbcac51. This is an OPTIMIZATION, not a correctness bug: the current behaviour is deliberate and pinned by tests/core-py/test_slonet_kv_cache.py::test_resolve_identical_prompt_falls_back ("same prompt -> degenerate case -> falls back to fresh").

MEASURED (live :8000, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, 482-token prompt, temperature=0):
- turn 1 (cold), session=ext-A .............. 16.48s
- turn 2 EXTENDS turn 1, same session ........ 1.96s   <- reuse works
- turn 2 same messages, COLD session ........ 19.38s   <- full prefill
- repeat the SAME 482-token prompt, warm ..... ~16s    <- header says: no gain

WHY: SloTransformer._resolve_kv_state (domain/training/_internal/slonet.py:6003) walks the shared prefix to `s`, then:
    if 0 < s < prompt_len: start = s
    else: start = 0
When the new prompt is IDENTICAL to the cached one, s walks all the way to prompt_len, the strict `<` fails, and start=0 — the entire 482-token prefill is recomputed even though the KV for nearly all of it is sitting in the session state. Verified at unit level (no model): prev=[1,2,3,4] -> identical prompt start=0, +1 token start=4, diverge at idx1 start=1, disjoint start=0.

WHY IT MATTERS: a retried request, a client resending the same context, or an agent loop that re-submits an unchanged prompt pays the full prefill every time (482 tokens ~= 16s on this box). Related: card 20261102_001621 (chat/generate repeats the completed block) shows repeat submissions are plausible in practice.

PROPOSED (one line, no new machinery): allow a full-prefix match to resume at prompt_len - 1, i.e. recompute ONLY the last prompt token, which is exactly what an incremental decode step does and is required anyway to produce logits for the next token:
    if 0 < s: start = min(s, prompt_len - 1)
    else: start = 0
The CV backends already handle arbitrary start>0 (the s<prompt_len path is in production); `state.backend.lens[:] = [start]` resets the fill length so the recomputed token's K/V overwrites the stale one. Expected: a repeat of a 482-token prompt drops from ~16s to roughly one decode step.

NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — needs approval + a benchmark (AGENTS.md: inference changes run scripts/benchmark_slonet.py / benchmark_latency.py) before it lands. The pinning test must be updated in the same commit, and its docstring should say WHICH card changed the contract.

ACCEPTANCE: replaying an identical prompt on a warm session is measurably faster than a cold session on the same prompt, with output byte-identical to the current full-recompute path (extend tests/core-py/test_slonet_kv_cache.py::TestCrossTurnGenerateNumpy::test_fresh_vs_reuse_same_input to cover the now-resuming case); no regression in benchmark_slonet.py.

── IMPLEMENTED + MEASURED 2026-11-02 (landed on main as 959484af8) ──

FIX: `_resolve_kv_state` had `if 0 < s < prompt_len: start = s else: start = 0`. A full-prompt match (s == prompt_len) therefore fell back to a full re-prefill. Now `if 0 < s: start = min(s, prompt_len - 1)` — exactly one token is recomputed, which is what an ordinary incremental decode step does and is required anyway because the final token's logits are never stored. Same function serves generate_numpy and generate_numpy_stream, so the stream path (what /v1 actually uses) is covered by the same change.

A/B ON THE REAL MODEL (Qwen2.5-0.5B .slnc, 482-token prompt, in-process, same weights, temperature=0, model load excluded; unchanged tree vs the branch):

                       before      after
  cold (empty state)   42.98s     49.69s
  repeat (warm state)  43.02s      1.26s   <- the path this card is about
  fresh (no state)     44.51s     43.62s

~34x on the repeat path. Output identity is asserted, not assumed: cold == repeat == fresh in both trees (and repeat == fresh is now a test for both the non-stream and the stream path).

TESTS: the degenerate case was pinned on purpose (`test_resolve_identical_prompt_falls_back`), so the pin was UPDATED, not deleted — renamed `test_resolve_identical_prompt_resumes_at_the_last_token`, asserting start == prompt_len - 1 and kv_len reset to it. Added `test_identical_prompt_resume_matches_fresh` and `test_identical_prompt_stream_resume_matches_fresh`, because nothing previously executed a full-prompt resume and /v1 is served by generate_numpy_stream.

GATES: 175 passed (test_slonet_kv_cache, test_slonet_generate, test_slonet_session_ttl, test_slonet_kv_benchmark, /v1 router, test_response_cache); scripts/benchmark_slonet.py all 7 benchmarks PASS (gradient_flow, training_convergence, export_import_roundtrip, accelerator_speed, lstm_forward_backward_speed, inference_consistency, transformer_vs_pytorch); ruff check + format clean.

NOTE ON A FLAKE SEEN ONCE: test_slonet_kv_benchmark.py::test_two_turn_speedup asserts wall-clock (`total_cached <= total_fresh * 1.5`) on a tiny model and failed once in a combined run (0.62x), then passed 3/3 alone and 2/2 in the same combined set, and also passed on the pre-change tree. It is timing noise, not this change — but a wall-clock assertion is the wrong gate for a cache. Deserves its own card: assert recomputed-token counts (deterministic) and report wall clock as output only.

COMPANION: this makes a warm PREFIX cheap (~1 token). It does not skip the model call — that is the response-cache layer (domain/inference/_internal/response_cache.py, exact sha256 tier, deterministic-only), which is wired in ChatDomain.respond but NOT in /v1 or /infer.
title: perf(inference): a repeated identical prompt re-prefills from scratch — /v1 session_id gains nothing when the prompt is unchanged

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 while verifying the /v1 session_id KV reuse (landed in 3dbcac51).

THE GAP: `SloNetServer.generate()` has two branches. When a ProcessGuard is attached AND alive (the default: config get_process_guard_enabled() is True, boot logs "Lazy-guard autoload: ProcessGuard started (THREAD mode, pre-loaded provider)"), it delegates:
    result = self._process_guard.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=..., temperature=..., ...)
and **session_id is not forwarded**. Even if it were, the worker side cannot use it as a KV key:
- ProcessGuard.generate (domain/infrastructure/_internal/process_guard.py:648) -> ThreadWorker.generate:172 mints its OWN `session_id = _new_session_id()` for IPC reply correlation, unrelated to the caller's KV session; the payload dict carries only max_new_tokens/temperature/top_p/top_k/repetition_penalty.
- ThreadWorker._generate_fn (process_guard.py:367) calls `model.generate_numpy(input_ids, ...)` with **no kv_state** at all.

So a direct `SloNetChatProvider.chat(...)` with a live guard silently forfeits cross-turn reuse — the exact silent-no-op class this port just fixed at the /v1 boundary.

NOT BROKEN TODAY: /v1 is unaffected. ProviderRouter.chat delegates to chat_stream (router.py:175's comment pins that), so /v1 traffic goes provider.chat_stream -> SloNetServer.generate_stream -> _generate_stream_sync(pump) -> SloNetServer._resolve_kv_state, which DOES honour session_id. Measured proof: with 8 /v1 requests served, GET /models/process-guard reported health.requests_served == 1 (the boot warmup only) — /v1 never entered the guard branch. Live reuse confirmed: turn-2-extends-turn-1 on the same session = 1.96s vs 19.38s cold.

WHY CARD IT ANYWAY: /v1 non-stream only escapes the guard branch by accident of going through chat_stream. `GET /models/process-guard` says the guard is the active execution path, and any future caller that (a) calls SloNetChatProvider.chat directly or (b) starts sending session_id on /infer (routers/infer.py:244) or /generate (routers/inference.py:1186) gets a silent no-op instead of an error. Also means guard-mode and non-guard-mode generation are not the same code path, which is a merge trap.

FIX SKETCH (needs approval; it touches the IPC contract, so it is a brief not a one-liner):
1. Split the two ids explicitly: keep `_new_session_id()` as the IPC correlation id, add `kv_session_id = kwargs.get("session_id")` to the payload dict in ThreadWorker.generate/generate_stream and in the subprocess worker equivalent.
2. ThreadWorker._generate_fn: resolve `provider._resolve_session_kv(kv_session_id)` (mirroring SloNetServer._resolve_kv_state) when a provider is bound, and pass `kv_state=` + `quantize_kv=` into `model.generate_numpy` / `generate_numpy_stream`.
3. SloNetServer.generate guard branch: forward `session_id=session_id`.
4. Test at the guard seam with a fake worker: same session_id twice must resolve the SAME kv_state object; a None session_id must resolve None. Assert the object identity, not just that a call happened (the lesson from bbcfafba1's reset_accelerator bug: count calls and you miss which state was served).

CONSTRAINT: the worker is the crash-isolation boundary — KV state lives in the worker process, so per-session state must be owned there (not in the parent), and the TTL/LRU eviction currently in SessionKVManager has to exist on that side too. Do not simply re-send buffers over IPC.

notes.text: DONE (ce29c13e2, format follow-up a4999b40f). Root cause: two ids travel the worker queue — _new_session_id() pairs IPC replies, the caller session_id keys cross-turn KV — and the caller id was dropped at both the server->guard hop and in the worker payload, so generate_numpy got kv_state=None every turn. Fix: payload built by _payload() (shared by generate/generate_stream), caller id rides as kv_session_id, _session_kv() resolves via provider._resolve_session_kv; HF mode keeps fresh state. Evidence: 196 passed (test_process_guard, test_slonet_server, llm_v1 router, guard controller), 7 new tests, scripts/benchmark_slonet.py all PASS.

title: fix(guard): SloNetServer.generate() drops session_id on the process-guard branch — cross-turn KV reuse is a silent no-op for direct provider.chat() callers

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 while landing card 20261102_012822 (identical-prompt KV resume).

test_slonet_kv_benchmark.py::TestCrossTurnBenchmark::test_two_turn_speedup ends with:
    assert total_cached <= total_fresh * 1.5, "KV cache should not be slower"
i.e. it gates on WALL CLOCK of a 1-block, 64-dim model where a single turn is a few milliseconds. Observed once in a combined run: 0.62x -> FAILED. Then: 3/3 passes alone, 2/2 passes in the exact same combined set, and a pass on the pre-change tree (origin/main) running the same four files. So it is scheduling noise, not a regression — but it fails for reasons unrelated to the property it names, which is the same "gate that does not test what its name says" trap as the ported reset_accelerator test.

WHY IT IS THE WRONG GATE FOR A CACHE: a cache's correctness property is HOW MUCH WORK IT SKIPPED, which is exact and cheap to assert; elapsed time is an environment measurement with a noise floor comparable to the signal on a tiny model.

PROPOSED: assert on recomputed tokens instead of milliseconds. _resolve_kv_state already returns `start` and `_prefill = prompt_len - start`; expose the per-call recomputed length (a counter on the state, or read kv_len before/after) and assert:
    turn2_recomputed == 1        (extension by exactly 1 token)
    repeat_recomputed == 1       (full-prompt match, after 20261102_012822)
    cold_recomputed == prompt_len
Keep printing the timings for humans (the suite's docstring already says it is a benchmark, run with -s), just do not assert on them. No threshold, no flake.

SCOPE: tests/core-py/test_slonet_kv_benchmark.py only. Do not touch generate/generate_numpy — the counter must be observation, not new production state, if it can be avoided (kv_len and the returned start already carry the answer).

CLOSED 2026-11-03: fixed by e0ac6ab16 — asserts recomputed token counts instead of wall clock; 60 passed x3, ruff clean.

description:
apps/api/server/main.py _install_stack_dump_timer (line ~234) / _cancel_stack_dump_timer (~259). faulthandler.dump_traceback_later periodic dumper was root-caused as the SIGSEGV trigger. User ruling at time: keep the dumper, dump CURRENT THREAD only — then shelved after it was shown dump_traceback_later has no all_threads parameter, and a current-thread-only dump from the timer thread would just print the timer's own useless stack. Real options to record: (a) Python-level fix: schedule the dumper on a timer but have it walk sys._current_frames() and write each thread's traceback via faulthandler.dump_traceback(file) — per-thread dumps without faulthandler's C-level all-threads walk, (b) drop the periodic timer entirely and dump only synchronously from signal handlers / on-watchdog, (c) keep as-is if a later repro disproves the causality. Evidence + repro steps from the original diagnosis session should be re-checked before choosing (this was shelved, not verified to root). DoD: reproduce or disprove, land the chosen mechanism with a test, remove the shelved state.

## Resolution 2026-11-02 — proven, fixed, landed (option a)

**Root cause CONFIRMED by core dumps** (crash reproduced live, no need to re-check old notes):
- 23 SIGSEGVs over 2026-10-31..11-02; crash cadence every 4-14 min (tonight 01:30:48, 01:39:21, 01:43:01, 01:53:13); one hit during IDLE STARTUP — no traffic required. systemd auto-restarts, so the service "looks up" while requests hang.
- 3 retained cores (pids 419307, 84130, 106351) all die at the IDENTICAL instruction: frame#0 `python3.12 + 0x1a3c7b` → `dump_frame`, `Python/traceback.c:1259` (`code->co_filename` off a foreign thread's already-torn-down frame).
- Mechanism: the periodic timer's C-level walk of raw `_PyInterpreterFrame` runs in signal/timer context WITHOUT the GIL and races normal frame teardown (GIL-governed frame lifetime).
- numba ruled out: installed Nov 1 13:10, first SEGVs Oct 31.

**Fix landed: `392fa637a`** (branch fix/fault-periodic-dumper-gil-safety) — periodic timer replaced with a daemon thread snapshotting `sys._current_frames()` (taken under GIL; frame objects pin the chain). On-crash faulthandler in `infrastructure/startup.py` untouched. 8 new contract tests (`tests/server/test_stack_dump.py`); gate: ruff clean, `tests/server/` 2037 passed / 1 skipped.

**Deployed:** slough-api restarted 02:53:46 WAT on 392fa637a; log line `stack dump active every 30.0s (SLO_DUMP_STACKS=1, gil-safe)`; 30s dump ticks present in journal.

**DoD remaining:** clean journal window — baseline is a crash every 4-14 min, so 30-60 min without `status=11/SEGV` is meaningful evidence. Then close.

description:
SCOPE: apps/api/server/routers/llm_v1.py + apps/api/server/routers/health.py + tests.

FOUND 2026-11-02 while closing 20261102_012822. ResponseCache (domain/inference/_internal/response_cache.py) exists, is tested, and is wired in exactly ONE caller: ChatDomain.respond. /v1 and /infer never touch it, so a repeated deterministic request on the external wire re-runs the model even though the answer is a pure function of the inputs. The KV work landed today makes a warm prompt 1.26s; a response-cache hit is milliseconds. Different tiers, both worth having.

THE LADDER (agreed with the user before implementation; total function, first match wins, every ambiguous case falls to "generate" because a wrong miss costs latency and a wrong hit costs correctness, invisibly):

  1. stream            -> generate (a hit is not a stream; replay is a separate contract)
  2. temperature > 0.2 -> generate (output is not a function of the inputs)
  3. tools/tool_choice -> generate (the real input is the tool result, not the prompt)
  4. hidden context not in the key -> generate
  5. exact key hit     -> serve, tagged cached=true
  7. otherwise         -> generate, then store

Rule 6 (semantic paraphrase tier) is DELIBERATELY not wired: similarity may propose a candidate but must never decide. A test asserts a paraphrase MISSES, so re-enabling it requires arguing for it rather than flipping a flag. No key laundering either - a replay is never re-stored under a new key.

KEY COMPLETENESS is the whole correctness argument, so the key must cover every input that can change the output: messages, model id, temperature, max_tokens, top_p, top_k AS SENT (top_k=0 maps to 40 in _sampling, so the effective value is keyed or two identical requests miss each other), stop (ignored today, keyed so honouring it later cannot collide), and session_id (it selects a KV state; a non-matching state falls back to full prefill, which the tests pin as output-identical). The generation token already covers model load/unload/swap.

OBSERVABILITY: an unobservable cache becomes an unexplained latency cliff. get_stats() goes on health.health_summary (the status-bar surface) behind a try/except that can never break health.

OUT OF SCOPE, card separately: /infer (different envelope, same seam), semantic tier enablement, intent->solver routing (Rung C), cross-session prefix table (Rung A).

── IMPLEMENTED + MEASURED 2026-11-02 (landed on main as ebb79bd83, docs a2d748c01) ──

WHAT LANDED: apps/api/server/routers/llm_v1.py now runs non-stream requests through the response-cache ladder before the engine. `_cache_key()` IS the ladder — a total function, first match wins, documented in its docstring so the next session reads the rule rather than reverse-engineering it:

    stream              -> generate (a hit is not a stream; replay is its own contract)
    temperature > 0.2   -> generate (output is not a function of the inputs)
    tools / tool_choice -> generate (the real input is the tool result, not the prompt)
    otherwise           -> exact key; hit -> replay tagged cached=true, miss -> generate then store

Every ambiguous case falls to "generate" on purpose: a wrong miss costs latency, a wrong hit costs correctness and is invisible (the replay is fluent either way).

RULE 6 (paraphrase/semantic tier) IS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED. similarity may propose a candidate but must never decide one. test_paraphrase_is_not_promoted posts "2+3" then "4+12" and asserts BOTH reach the engine — so turning the semantic tier on for /v1 requires deleting an argument, not flipping a flag. No key laundering either: a replay is never re-stored under another prompt's key.

KEY COMPLETENESS (the whole correctness argument): messages, model id, temperature, max_tokens, top_p, top_k AS SENT (note: _sampling maps top_k=0 -> 40, so keying the raw 0 would make two identical requests miss each other), stop (phase 1 ignores it, keyed anyway so honouring it later cannot collide), session_id (selects a KV state; a non-matching state falls back to full prefill, pinned output-identical by test_slonet_kv_cache). The module's generation token covers model load/unload/swap.

NEW WIRE FIELDS: ChatBody.tools / ChatBody.tool_choice, declared so the ladder can SEE a tool turn instead of silently caching one. Same convention as the existing `stop` field ("Accepted; phase 1 ignores"). CHAT_SPEC.descriptor untouched -> gen_router_manifest --check and gen_ts_contracts --check both report up to date.

OBSERVABILITY: ResponseCache.get_stats() is exposed on health.health_summary (the status-bar surface) behind a try/except that can never break health. Cache hits record 0 model tokens in record_inference, so tokens/s is not inflated by work nobody did. Hits also log at INFO and write an audit row with cached=1.

MEASURED (scripts/benchmark_response_cache.py, extended rather than duplicated — the file already existed from commit 51d3a60ac and I initially CLOBBERED it, then restored it from HEAD and added a /v1 section):
    build_key[33 msgs]          88.26 us/op
    v1_gate_hit_check           32.49 us/op     (ladder + exact lookup)
    v1_replay_shape              5.72 us/op     (wire payload shaping)
    get[hit]                     0.74 us/op
    -> full /v1 replay ~82 us, verdict PASS (<1 ms budget)
For scale, the same 482-token prompt on the real model: 1.26 s from a warm KV state, 43.02 s from an empty one (card 20261102_012822). So a replay is ~15,000x a warm KV resume and ~520,000x a cold prefill.

TESTS (10 new, apps/api/server/tests/test_llm_v1_router.py::TestResponseCacheLadder): replay happens and is shaped identically to the generated response; replay is tagged and generation is not; stochastic always generates (+bypass counter); streaming neither reads nor fills the tier (+bypass counter); top_p is in the key; top_k keyed as sent (0 == 40, 40 != 20); session_id in the key; generation bump invalidates; tool-carrying request never replayed; paraphrase not promoted. Plus TestCacheObservability: hit_rate/generation present on the health snapshot, and the snapshot returns {} instead of raising when the cache is unavailable.

GATES: 247 passed (llm_v1 router, response_cache, semantic_cache, chat_domain, chat_domain2, health router, contracts); scripts/benchmark_slonet.py all 7 PASS (gradient_flow, training_convergence, export_import_roundtrip, accelerator_speed, lstm_forward_backward_speed, inference_consistency, transformer_vs_pytorch); ruff check + format clean; manifest + TS contracts up to date.

HONEST LIMITATION: /v1's default temperature is 0.7, which is > 0.2, so the cache only engages for clients that ask for determinism (temperature <= 0.2) and do not stream. That is the correct default — a stochastic request is not a function of its inputs — but it means this is a win for eval/agent/benchmark traffic, not for chat traffic. Widening it means changing the determinism threshold, which is a separate argument.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: cross-session prefix table (same token prefix, different client); /infer parity; intent->solver routing for genuinely different prompts with the same answer.
title: perf(inference): /v1 has no response cache — a repeated deterministic prompt still runs the model

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 while landing 20261102_021851 (/v1 response cache).

THE GAP: cross-turn KV reuse is keyed by session_id (SessionKVManager -> KVState._sessions). Two clients — or one client reconnecting, or two routes — that send the SAME 400-token system prompt each pay full prefill for it, because their session ids differ. The prefix comparison itself already exists and returns the shared length (KVState.session_get returns (past_key_values, prefix_len), and prefix_match() walks the ids); only the LOOKUP KEY is per-session.

THE MECHANISM: a content-addressed prefix table. Hash block-aligned token prefixes (e.g. every 32/64 tokens), store the paged K/V blocks under the hash in a global LRU, and on a session miss fall back to a prefix-hash lookup before prefill. This is vLLM's automatic prefix caching, and it is the honest reading of "identical but a different route": the route differs, the tokens up to a point do not.

WHY IT IS SAFE (unlike the semantic tier): K/V is a pure function of the token ids and their positions, so a block-aligned prefix hit is token-exact by construction. No threshold, no similarity, no wrong-answer class — the only hazard is a hash collision, which a full-prefix comparison on hit removes.

MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD PROVE IT: two different session_ids, same 400-token prefix, second request timed against a cold prefill on the real model. Reference points already on the board: 43.02 s cold, 1.26 s warm for 482 tokens (card 20261102_012822).

OUT OF SCOPE: response-level replay (that is 20261102_021851, answer tier), /infer parity (separate card), and any cross-token reuse — K/V cannot be transplanted between different token sequences, and pretending otherwise produces fluent wrong output.

notes.author: opencode
notes.text: LANDED e15691d54 (rebased; main 8666f46de) (branch perf/kv-prefix-cache). PrefixCache: content-addressed (blake2b over token ids) LRU of block-aligned KV snapshots; adopt on session miss, harvest at generation end FROM THE RAW BUFFERS so the session-less /v1 client also contributes (harvesting only kv_state objects would have saved nothing: a session already resumes from its own KV). Dims/quantize mismatch refused; copies never aliased; table dropped on load_state_dict; SLO_KV_PREFIX_CACHE=0 kills it live; prefix_cache_stats() on health.health_summary as kv_prefix_cache. BENCH scripts/benchmark_kv_prefix_cache.py (4L/256d, 256-token, fresh state each iter): cold 91.25ms -> warm-from-table 7.65ms = 91.6% prefill saved; table ops 6.5/10.1/17.6us (exact/partial/store). TESTS 20 new, incl. bit-identical adopt in float32 AND int8 K/V (int8 = what quantized prod models use); kv+state+session suites 42 passed; benchmark_slonet 7/7 PASS; ruff clean.

title: perf(kv): prefix cache is keyed by session_id — two clients with the same token prefix both re-prefill

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 while landing 20261102_021851 (/v1 response cache).

/v1 now replays repeated deterministic requests; /infer (routers/infer.py -> InferRouter -> the same provider seam) still does not, and neither does the chat router for anything outside ChatDomain.respond.

DiFFERENT ENVELOPE, SAME LADDER: reuse routers.llm_v1._cache_key rather than re-deriving the rule, so there is ONE ladder. What differs is the response envelope and the key surface (InferRequest's own sampling fields — include every one of them in `extra`, or two requests differing only in one of them collide).

WHY IT MATTERS: /infer is what the local UI and internal tooling call, so it is the path most likely to replay the same prompt during benchmark/eval loops — exactly the traffic the cache is for (temperature <= 0.2, non-stream).

SCOPE: no new endpoint, no new cache; projection of the existing tier. Test only the seam (provider called once for two identical deterministic requests; twice when a sampling param differs).
title: feat(inference): /infer has no response cache — reuse the /v1 ladder instead of re-deriving it

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 from the user's question: "2+3 = 5 and 4+12 = 5 — how do we resume identical-but-different-route?"

THE DECISION RECORDED: they are not the same request and must not share a cache entry. They share an ANSWER SHAPE, not an answer; and if both really equal 5, one is wrong. Answer-level reuse of a correct computation is safe ("the value is 5"); reusing the DERIVATION across different inputs is not caching at all — it is amortized reasoning.

WHAT WOULD BE CORRECT: classify the intent, route arithmetic / unit conversion / lookup to a solver, and cache the evaluator's (expression -> value) mapping, which is exact by construction. The LLM then explains a computed fact instead of recalling one. For the literal arithmetic case this removes the wrong-answer class entirely rather than making it fast.

BLOCKED ON A PRODUCT CALL, not on code: which intents may bypass the model. A wrong classification is a wrong answer, so the allowlist is the deliverable and it needs an owner. Do not build the router before the allowlist.

RELATED AND ALSO DECIDED: the semantic paraphrase tier stays OFF for serving paths. In semantic_cache.py the match is content-word Jaccard (>=80% of the query's content words) boosted by HD similarity, threshold 0.85; a single-content-word query ("continue", "yes") scores 0.95 against every variant of itself regardless of what context the cached answer depended on. Similarity may PROPOSE a candidate; it may never DECIDE one. router tests pin that a paraphrase misses (test_paraphrase_is_not_promoted).
title: product(inference): route arithmetic/lookup intents to a solver instead of caching across different prompts
