description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 ~02:55 by querying the Actions API directly (gh auth is VALID: account iamtowbee, token scopes gist/read:org/read:packages/repo — the older "gh token invalid" note is stale).

THE PROBLEM: CI on main never reaches a verdict. In the ~2.5 hours before this card, main produced ONE success (00:26, which cleared only because there was a ~20 minute gap between pushes) and 24 consecutive `cancelled` runs. The 02:40 run is the clearest specimen: 7 of 8 jobs COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY (TypeScript, Frontend unit tests, Vite build, Board integrity, Python 3.11, Python 3.12, Feature Tags) while E2E tests sat in `npm run e2e:vite` for 15+ minutes; then a newer push cancelled the whole run ("Canceling since a higher priority waiting request for CI-refs/heads/main exists"). So the per-job gates are fine and fast — Python finishes in ~1-2 min — but main is structurally unable to conclude.

ROOT CAUSE (two independent multipliers):
  1. .github/workflows/ci.yml has `on.push.branches: [main]` with NO paths filter, so bookkeeping commits ("kanban: sync ...", docs/sync) start the full suite.
  2. `concurrency: group: CI-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true` — correct for PRs (a new push should supersede the old one) and wrong for main (every run is a distinct commit that needs its own verdict). Combined with the repo's 1-5 minute push cadence from parallel sessions, every run is superseded before E2E finishes.

FIX (cheapest first):
  1. `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}` — main serializes, PRs still cancel-and-replace. This is the one-line fix that makes main verdicts exist.
  2. Add `paths-ignore: ['.kanban/**', 'docs/**', '**.md', '*.txt']` to the push trigger. A kanban sync commit does not need E2E, and right now the bookkeeping traffic is what kills the real runs.
  3. Split `frontend-e2e` into its own workflow so a slow E2E cannot hold the unit/type/python verdicts hostage; E2E status then becomes a separate required check instead of a shared cancellation domain.
  4. While in there: every actions/*@v4 in these workflows logs "Node.js 20 is deprecated ... forced to run on Node.js 24", and ubuntu-latest migrates to Ubuntu 26 (Oct 19 2026 notice). Bump action versions deliberately, in their own commit, and re-pin node-version where the toolchain actually depends on it.

NOT DONE THIS SESSION (user was wrapping up): no workflow edits, because a CI config change needs a run to validate and there was no quiet window.

HOW TO CHECK IT LANDED: after the change, `gh run list --workflow=ci.yml -L 10` on main should show `success`/`failure` per commit with no `cancelled` beyond the newest; and a docs-only commit should not start a run at all.

notes.author: opencode
notes.text: VERDICT 2026-11-02 10:45 — the fix holds. Main now concludes per commit instead of cancelling: CI run 41417458193 (8666f46de) success, 41422832531 (8ff6f3432) success; no `cancelled` runs since. What stayed red was CI/CD (deploy half), and it was NOT this card: (a) a router `domain.*._internal` reach-in introduced by the /v1 response-cache work failed three separate gates (tests/test_router_domain_facade, tests/contract/test_router_boundary, tests/test_layer_conformance) plus docs-api parity — fixed in 11e3b9eaf by exporting ResponseCache/get_response_cache from domain.inference; (b) domain-baseline drift — fixed in bf84b8f96; (c) two CI-only test seams (fake-cupy driver probe, response-tracker singleton) — fixed in 3538e9b95, cards 20261102_103738 x2. Still open from the original description, deliberately: split frontend-e2e into its own workflow (a slow E2E should not share a cancellation domain with the fast verdicts) and bump actions/*@v4 (Node 20 deprecation / Ubuntu 26 migration).

title: ci(github): CI on main never concludes — 24 consecutive cancellations, cancel-in-progress kills every run

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 by a cleanup sweep (ratchet green, F401 clean, full rule set clean).

THE GAP: .github/workflows/ci_cd.yml lints only two trees —
    ruff check packages/core-py/ apps/api/server/
    ruff format --check packages/core-py/ apps/api/server/
Everything else (domain/, journeys/, packages/* except core-py, apps/cli, apps/web server code, scripts/, tests/) is ungated. That is how a genuine I001 in scripts/finetune_gpt2.py survived: it was invisible to CI and only surfaced when someone ran ruff over the whole tree by hand.

MEASURED 2026-11-02 with the full tree (domain journeys packages apps scripts, 1383 files):
  ruff check  -> CLEAN after pinning known-third-party = ["datasets"] (b9cde163e)
  ruff format --check -> 46 files would be reformatted

THE 46 ARE REAL DRIFT, NOT NEW BREAKAGE: pre-commit runs `ruff format` on staged *.py, so every file anyone touches is auto-reformatted — the untouched remainder simply fell behind over months. Distribution: domain/infrastructure/_internal (10), scripts (11), apps/cli/src (9), packages/* (6), domain/shell (5), domain/training (2), root benchmark_results.py, etc.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN THE SWEEP: a 46-file mechanical reformat is exactly the mass-edit AGENTS.md forbids doing opportunistically — it touches 10+ worktree-live areas while parallel sessions push every few minutes, and it would produce a large diff with zero behaviour change at the same moment as real work is in flight.

THE FIX (one deliberate pass, quiet window):
  1. `ruff format domain journeys packages apps scripts` in a commit that contains NOTHING else, so the large diff is its own reviewable unit.
  2. Widen the CI step to the same tree in the same PR, so the drift cannot recur.
  3. Verify with `ruff format --check` over the full tree -> 0, and confirm `ruff check` stays clean.
  4. Then the gate is honest: what CI checks equals what the repo is.

NOT IN SCOPE: format-on-save churn, prettier for TS (separate toolchain), and the Node 20 / Ubuntu 26 action bumps (card 20261102_025758 follow-up).
title: ci(lint): ruff gates cover only 2 of 7 trees — 46 files of format drift are ungated

description:
SHIPPED (branch fix/voice-input-duplication, commit 55394d7cf, 1 commit off origin/main).

ROOT CAUSE: apps/web/features/chat/components/input/VoiceInput.tsx onresult re-joined ALL results from index 0 on every recognition event and emitted the whole utterance; ChatInput.handleVoiceTranscript APPENDS (`${value} ${text}`) then auto-sends via pendingSendRef. Event N therefore emitted results[0..N] on top of text already holding results[0..N-1] -> multiplicative composer growth. Emitting interim fragments additionally pushed half-finished words into the append+auto-send path.

FIX: walk from event.resultIndex (added to the local SpeechRecognitionEvent interface) and keep isFinal results only -- mirrors the proven loop in features/chat/voice/speech-engine.ts:350-363, which was already the correct in-repo pattern. ChatInput's append semantic is unchanged and is now correct: each final utterance lands exactly once.

NOT DONE HERE (deferred, by design): ChatInput's stale-closure guard in handleVoiceTranscript. With isFinal-only emission there is one emit per listening session and value cannot change mid-session, so the stale capture is currently harmless -- but it is still a latent hazard if interim emission returns.

GATES: vitest 20/20 (VoiceInput 11 incl. 3 new, ChatInput 9 incl. the seam contract), tsc --noEmit 0, eslint 0 errors (3 pre-existing warnings: unused onSend arg + 2x addToast deps).

New tests: (1) interim never emitted; (2) bug repro -- 3 partial events replacing result[0] in place -> exactly 1 emission of 'hello world'; (3) new final segment emitted alone, never re-joined as 'hello there'; (4) ChatInput appends each final transcript exactly once.
title: fix(chat): VoiceInput transcript duplication loop on partial results

description:
Observed in journal/network logs during the meta-weight investigation (2026-11-01), separate from both chat-loop bugs.

SYMPTOM: the frontend issues PATCH /settings/generation roughly every 3 seconds with an IDENTICAL payload, alongside polling the deprecated GET /config/generation. Neither the value nor anything server-side is changing -- it is a write loop, not a reaction to change.

WHY IT MATTERS: (1) pointless write traffic + audit/log noise on a state that is not mutating; (2) a periodic identical PUT/PATCH can mask a REAL settings change in the noise (and can race/overwrite a concurrent edit from another tab or the API); (3) GET /config/generation is deprecated -- it should not be in the polling set at all.

EXPECTED: poll only when the value can actually change (server-driven updates, or focus/visibility re-sync), skip the write when the payload is byte-identical to the last acknowledged value, and drop the deprecated endpoint in favour of the current settings contract.

SCOPE: frontend settings/generation only. Do NOT touch generation params semantics, the meta-weight band (fix/meta-weight-band), or VoiceInput (fix/voice-input-duplication).

Acceptance: no identical-payload PATCH in steady state (assertable in a test with a fake timer); deprecated GET /config/generation gone from the polling path; a real settings change still round-trips and is reflected in the UI.
title: perf(web): settings generation polling spams PATCH/GET every ~3s

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 ~10:30 in CI/CD run 41422832686 (8ff6f3432), job test-core-py.

5 reds, all TestCudaWithFakeCupy: test_cuda_available_with_fake_cupy,
test_cuda_dtype_fp32_and_fp16, test_cuda_to_from_device_with_fake_cupy,
test_cuda_vram_full_tier, test_cuda_vram_lite_tier.

THE BUG IS THE TEST, NOT THE MODEL. `_CUDABackend.is_available()` first calls
`_cuda_driver_present()` (dlopen libcuda.so.1) and returns False before it ever
imports cupy. GitHub runners have no libcuda, so the fake-cupy module installed by
monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, 'cupy', ...) is never reached: is_available() is
False, _cp stays None (-> AttributeError: 'NoneType' has no attribute float32), and
vram_gb() falls back to 4.0 (-> tier 'lite' vs asserted 'full').

Proof of the environment dependency: the same 183 tests pass locally, because this
dev box HAS libcuda.so.1 installed (no GPU needed for dlopen to succeed) while CI
does not. So the suite is green on the machine that writes it and red on the machine
that gates it — the worst split.

FIX: the class tests the cupy dispatch arm, not driver probing, so pin the seam:
a class-level autouse fixture monkeypatching slib._cuda_driver_present -> True.
Driver probing keeps its own coverage (test_slolib_gpu has direct probes).

WHY IT BLOCKS: CI/CD has been red on main for every push in this window, so the
deploy half of the pipeline cannot go green and real regressions hide behind it.

Verified under the CI condition (probe forced False): TestCudaWithFakeCupy 11 passed, previously 5 red. Driver probing keeps its own coverage elsewhere in the file; the fixture is monkeypatch-scoped, so nothing leaks to sibling tests.

description:
FOUND 2026-11-02 ~10:30 in CI/CD run 41422832686 (8ff6f3432), job test-core-py.

RED: TestReadResponseDocs::test_canonical_dir_with_empty_journal_returns_none —
`assert [...docs...] is None`, and the leaked docs are canned fixture text
('hi', 'capital of France?' -> 'The capital of France is Paris.').

THE MECHANISM: the test monkeypatches `_canonical_log_dir()` to a fresh tmp dir but
then calls read_response_docs(), which resolves the singleton via
`get_response_tracker()`. That singleton is process-global and lazily built on the
REAL canonical dir; whichever test file logged a response first leaves a populated
collection in it. The canonical-dir gate then passes (tmp == patched canonical), the
singleton hands back the other file's docs, and the 'empty journal' assertion sees
them. Passes in isolation (183/183 with test_slolib_gpu), fails only in the full run
— classic shared-mutable-singleton order dependency.

FIX: patch `_response_tracker` to a fresh ResponseTracker(log_dir=tmp) alongside
`_canonical_log_dir`, exactly like the sibling test_canonical_dir_returns_docs does.
The test's subject is 'empty collection -> None', which needs an empty collection,
not 'whatever the process happens to have cached'.

WHY IT BLOCKS: same as the gpu card — CI/CD red on main, deploy gated.

notes.author: opencode
notes.text: FIXED 3538e9b95. The test now patches `_response_tracker` to a fresh ResponseTracker(log_dir=tmp) alongside `_canonical_log_dir`, matching its sibling test_canonical_dir_returns_docs — the assertion is about an EMPTY collection, and the process-global singleton was answering with another file's docs. Verified against a deliberately pre-populated singleton: 29 passed. No product change: read_response_docs' behaviour is correct, the test simply never controlled its input.

description:
Two feedback->behaviour integrators exist and only the wrong one is live.

INTENDED (user ruling): feedback -> TraitWeightsConfig.update() -> managers read weights -> ContextCore applies -> prompt.
The pieces exist: domain/context/_internal/managers.py has TraitWeightsConfig (clamped [0,1] by construction, persisted
MogDB+JSON, snapshots, 5s cache) + Personality/Memory/Style/Task managers with apply(base_prompt);
domain/inference/_internal/context_contract.py owns ContextPart provenance + budget_parts + render_context_block;
ContextCore.build_context_frame is live in inference.py:614 and feedback/workflow.py:177 already calls update_from_feedback().
MISSING LINK: ContextCore.set_managers() has ONLY test callers, so _apply_managers() never runs in production and the frame
carries no trait steering.

DUPLICATE (accidental): domain/feedback/_internal/meta_weights.py integrates feedback into SAMPLER params
(_apply_meta_weights x4 in inference.py). Unbounded floats into a shared, model-agnostic gain -> rep 0.8 -> reward
repetition -> the loop in card 20261102_001621. Duplicates a responsibility TraitWeightsConfig already owns, one layer down.

SECOND DEFECT: context is injected at the HEAD (knowledge appended to system_prompt :1993, RAG messages.insert(0,...) :2020),
so the token prefix changes every turn and kills the KV prefix reuse measured at 43s -> 1.26s. Steady-state prefill is
re-paid per turn on a 482-token prompt.

Plan: (1) attach_managers(ctx_core, config) in domain/context + startup hook; (2) SLO_META_WEIGHT_NUDGE default off;
(3) stable head (system_prompt + agent instructions) vs volatile tail (knowledge/frame/RAG appended to the LAST user turn);
(4) tests: managers reflected in the frame, flag-off returns params unchanged, head bytes identical across turns with
different context, volatile block present at the tail only; (5) benchmark_latency/slonet before-after.
Supersedes 20261101_182428 (the two-bound-set question dissolves: bounded trait space is the authority; sampler nudge goes dark).
Evidence bar: same answer with feedback ON vs OFF for the count-1-to-10 prompt, and reused-token count preserved.

LANDED on main `e3fce3a01` (4 commits: 93f3b1196 feat, af67cfc2c/f019659ea-family + e3fce3a01 rehash/sync; fix commit 71ef98fa4).

STILL OPEN (needs a human decision, not code)

description:
Reproduced 2026-11-03 while landing 20261103_071231 (context steering).

`tests/test_rag_context_budget.py` inserts `apps/api/server` into sys.path and does
`from routers.inference import _RAG_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS, _build_rag_block`. In the same
pytest session, `tests/server/test_inference_router.py` imports the canonical
`apps.api.server.routers.inference`. Those are two distinct module objects with two
distinct `_instance` singletons and two distinct copies of module state.

Symptom: running the two files together fails 5 chat tests with
`Model not loaded` (E_INFRA_REGISTRY) — `TestChat::test_chat_success`,
`TestChatPostGenTasks` x3, `TestChatStreamCancel::test_cancel_event_reaches_provider`.
Each passes alone, and each passes with every other file in the closure.

PROVEN PRE-EXISTING: checked out HEAD (bd7f342e5) for all six files and the same
5 fail. Not a regression from the context-steering change.

Fix direction (one line, needs the import to be canonical): drop the sys.path hack
and `from apps.api.server.routers.inference import ...`. Verify `tests/server` +
`tests/test_rag_context_budget.py` in one process is green, then check nothing else
relied on the `routers.*` alias. Why it matters: a full-suite CI run collects both
files, so this class of dual-import poisoning makes the chat suite order-dependent
and its reds unattributable.

FIXED same session (2026-11-03): dropped the sys.path hack, import is now
`from apps.api.server.routers.inference import _RAG_CONTEXT_MAX_CHARS, _build_rag_block`
— one module object per session, so `_instance` and module state are the router the
rest of the suite drives.

Evidence: `tests/server/test_inference_router.py` + `tests/test_rag_context_budget.py`
in one process: **5 failed / 82 passed -> 87 passed** (RAG tests unchanged and still
green, so no behaviour was traded for isolation).

description:
FOUND 2026-11-03 by run 41591282369 (3fe9b43e0) — the first run in weeks where every test/lint job passed, so the build job finally ran: web image fails at [deps 5/7] RUN npm ci with ERESOLVE (react@^19.0.0 in apps/web/package.json vs react 18.3.1 in apps/web/package-lock.json; @react-three/fiber@^9.8.2 needs peer react >=19). ROOT CAUSE: fd86ab831 (2026-10-23, 3D kanban view) bumped apps/web/package.json to react ^19 + added r3f but never regenerated the NESTED lock (last touched e9209cbdf 2026-09-12). The ROOT workspace lock is in sync (react 19.3.0, fiber 9.8.2) and is what every CI job installs from — npm ci inside a workspace member climbs to the workspace root (ci.yml comment: 'ONE workspace-root install'), so test-web is green. Only consumers without a root package.json break: apps/web/Dockerfile copies just apps/web/package.json + nested lock into the image context, so npm treats apps/web as standalone and resolves the stale nested lock. cloudflare-pages.yml / deploy-git-sync.yml run npm ci in apps/web at full checkout → climb to root → work (their cache-dependency-path still points at the nested lock: stale cache key, fix in passing). FIX (one lock, one truth — the doctrine test-web/ci.yml already document): rework the Dockerfile deps stage to copy the root package.json + root package-lock.json + all four workspace package.jsons (workspaces: apps/web, packages/strui, packages/sdk-ts/typescript-sdk, packages/eslint-config) and npm ci --ignore-scripts at /app; builder stage carries root package.json + node_modules + apps/web + strui sources (strui exports raw TS src, no build step; --ignore-scripts proven by test-web which runs vite build off the same install). Nested lock becomes orphaned — follow-up card to delete it (not in this change). No docker locally: CI build job is the verifier; local dry-run = exact COPY set + npm ci + vite build in a temp dir.

description:
Measured on the live restart 2026-11-03 (journal, `from_slnc timing`):
  parse=0.01s model=0.01s weights=2.92s convert=0.00s load_state=0.11s total=3.05s
  then 09:17:24 -> 09:17:32 = ~8s to load model.slnc.quant.npz
  process start 09:16:57 -> model_loaded 09:17:37 = ~40s total

The 2.4 GB fp32 .slnc loads in 2.92s (mmap + parallel). The 421 MB
model.slnc.quant.npz takes ~8s because `Quantine.save_weights` uses
`np.savez_compressed` (DEFLATE on all 338 entries) and int8 weights are
high entropy: 505 MB raw -> 421 MB stored = only 1.15x, i.e. 84 MB saved
for 6.2s of single-threaded zlib (measured 82 MB/s warm on lm_head.npy).

Two defects in `Quantine.load_weights`:
1. Serial inflate. zlib releases the GIL, so the 169 arrays can be
   decompressed concurrently; nothing does.
2. `arr = np.asarray(arr).copy(order='C')` — np.load already returns a
   C-contiguous array, so this is a pure 505 MB copy (extra time + peak).

Fix: parallel inflate over N NpzFile handles (one per worker, split the
169 names into groups so each worker parses the central directory once)
+ copy only when not already C-contiguous. Keep npz_stored/mmap as the
alternative (B) only if disk allows — it costs +84 MB and disk is at 98%.

Expected: ~8s -> ~1-2s; peak RSS down ~0.5 GB transient.
Benchmark: scripts/benchmark_model_load.py (new) with a gate on total
load_weights wall time, run against the real Qwen2.5-0.5B artifact.
notes: LANDED 50d257e23 (tests: tests/core-py/test_quantization_coverage.py +5, 35 passed; benchmark: scripts/benchmark_model_load.py). Quantine.load_weights splits the 169 arrays across min(8, cpu_count) workers, one NpzFile per worker (zipfile serialises reads on a shared handle through its own lock, so one handle would be a race with no speedup; SLO_QUANT_LOAD_WORKERS overrides), interleaved so a 136 MB lm_head cannot serialise one chunk, merged deterministically in sorted order, and copies only when the array is not already C-contiguous (np.load returns C-contiguous writable arrays, so the old unconditional .copy(order='C') was a redundant 505 MB memcpy). Measured same-process, serial baseline then parallel back to back on this 4C/8T i5-9300H: 7.06 s -> 3.30 s (2.14x, gate 2.00x); 169 tensors, all C-contiguous; peak RSS 526 -> 533 MB with no second copy. The ceiling is zlib itself — raw zipfile inflation is 2.4-2.6 s at 4-8 workers, so ~3.3 s is the floor here. Artifact format untouched (savez_compressed kept); npz_stored/mmap rejected on the disk budget (+84 MB for ~6 s on a 99% full disk).
title: perf(quant): parallel DEFLATE inflate + drop the redundant copy in Quantine.load_weights

description:
Readiness is gated on inventory + background workflows. Measured cold start 2026-11-03
(journal 09:16:57 -> 09:17:37, 40s to model_loaded):
  imports                 3.1s   (526 modules, fastapi 1.86s)      unavoidable
  soul inventory scan    11-23s  <- THE BLANK: 09:17:00 -> 09:17:11
  feedback workflow       9s     <- 09:17:11 -> 09:17:20
  fp32 .slnc weights      2.9s   (2.5GB, mmap+parallel, already good)
  quant npz DEFLATE       8s     (separate card 20261103_082215)

DEFECT A: SloManager.__init__ -> _scan_souls() parses every candidate soul
synchronously on the event loop. _parse_soul_info reads the embedded JSON
config header and json.loads it: measured 2.21s for ONE 67MB config
(read 0.20s), and 23.34s for the real 25 candidates in models/
(10 files at 2.3-2.7s each). Deduped to 5 souls -> the observed 11s window.
A 67MB config is NOT needed to answer 'what souls exist'.
Fix: lazy scan (no scan in __init__), persisted (path, mtime, size) -> SloInfo
index at data/.soul_index.json, and a daemon warm thread from startup so the
first /souls request never pays it.

DEFECT B: main.py:178 calls _start_feedback_workflow() on the loop; it does
adapter aggregation (workflow.py:569, observed 9s) before returning. It is
background work riding the critical path.
Fix: run it on a daemon thread, same as the adjacent rag-init thread.

Also noted (not fixed here): 'Stage CRITICAL: complete (3/3 hooks OK, 0.0s
elapsed)' reports 0.0s for a 13s window - the stage timer is broken.

Gate: scripts/benchmark_startup.py cold-start -> /health 200, plus soul-scan
wall time from a cold index. Expect ~40s -> ~14s with card 20261103_082215.
notes: LANDED 179700abd (lazy+indexed scan) + 52c3b67c6 (boot threads) + 3f9c684db (benchmark). A: SloManager.__init__ no longer scans. _ensure_scanned() populates on first real use and data/.soul_index.json caches SloInfo keyed by (abspath, mtime_ns, size): rewritten files re-parse, deleted ones prune, unknown schema or corrupt JSON falls back to parsing. Construction 0.4-1.2 ms (was ~11 s); cold scan 11.85-13.0 s (one-time); warm index 10.8-12.8 ms (~940-1200x), same 5 souls on both paths. The index lives beside the souls dir unless that dir is the repo's models/ (then data/), so a test run can never rewrite production state. warm()/warm_soul_index_async() give boot a daemon warm thread (SLO_SOUL_INDEX_WARM=0 disables). B: _start_feedback_workflow() moved to a daemon thread named feedback-workflow (it did adapter aggregation, 9 s measured inline). Verified with scripts/benchmark_startup.py (spawn -> /health, full model): before ~40 s to ready; after 18.12 s ready / 7.78 s health with a warm index, 36.12 s / 14.52 s on a cold index, preload_warnings 0 in both runs. Bonus fix: get_trait_weights() re-read the config header with the version field as meta_len and failed on every call; it now reads the cached SloInfo traits. Gates: test_slo_manager 147 passed, test_quantization_coverage 35 passed, soul/quant/souls-router/startup-routers 237 passed, run_affected.sh tests/server tests/core-py 7206 passed / 1 skipped / 4 xfailed (1 Playwright browser error is environmental). Known residual: json.loads on the 41 MB soul config does not release the GIL, so a cold index still costs up to ~2.2 s of loop latency once — see the follow-up card for dropping metadata.training_state.optimizer at soul-write time.

LIVE RESTART, landed code (main b6b1dce07), slough-api.service 2026-11-03 11:59:25 WAT — the benchmark port and the real unit agree. Timeline from the journal: 11:59:25 server start / Stage CRITICAL; 11:59:28 all routers registered (66) + Phase 4 model load (background) + soul-index warm thread starts + SLNCParser reads model.slnc (2520.7 MB); 11:59:29 Stage READY + uvicorn serving (GET /health 200 measured externally at +13.7 s from the restart verb, which includes the stop of the old process); 11:59:36 feedback workflow on its daemon thread; 11:59:38 'Found 5 souls (0 parsed, 31 indexed, 10.22s)'; 11:59:43 from_slnc total=6.22s; 11:59:48 'Startup complete — server ready for requests' = ~23 s from process start vs ~40 s before the change. THE ORDERING IS THE PROOF: /health answered at 11:59:29, nine seconds BEFORE the soul inventory finished at 11:59:38 — inventory no longer gates readiness, it lands on its own thread. HONEST CAVEAT, not hidden: the warm scan measured 10.22 s here vs 12.8 ms in scripts/benchmark_soul_index.py. Work is 31 stats + a 35 KB index read (the models/ recursive glob is 9.7 ms and walks 323 entries, re-measured), so this is contention, not parsing: it overlaps the 2.5 GB .slnc read (weights=6.06 s this run vs 2.92 s idle) on one disk. It does not delay readiness, and _sync_soul_traits() in the PGQ model-load worker was not the gate either (the scan finished 5 s before 'Startup complete'). Consequence to keep in mind: an early /souls request can wait on _scan_lock for as long as that I/O contention lasts; the fix, if it ever bites, is reading the index before walking candidates (or bounding the walk), not moving the scan back onto the readiness path.
title: perf(startup): soul inventory scan + feedback workflow must not gate readiness

description:
A cold soul index still costs up to ~2.2 s of event-loop latency, once.

Measured 2026-11-03: one .soul config is 41 MB of JSON and json.loads(s) is
~2.2 s (read 0.20 s, parse 2.21 s). The parse does not release the GIL, so no
thread placement helps — the loop stalls for the duration regardless of
warm_soul_index_async(). Today only the FIRST boot after a soul changes pays
it (the index then makes it ~12 ms), and _sync_soul_traits() now runs inside
the PGQ model-load worker so the stall cannot block /health or the model load
ordering — but it is still a visible latency cliff for in-flight requests.

Root cause is not the reader, it is the writer: `metadata.training_state`
carries the full Adam optimizer state (exp_avg / exp_avg_sq moments) as JSON
floats, ~41 MB of text for a 5 MB model. Inventory only needs name/description/
traits/personality.

Fix (soul-write time, one owner): when saving a .soul, store
metadata.training_state.optimizer out-of-band (sidecar file next to the soul,
e.g. .soul.optim.npz) or strip it from the config header behind an explicit
`soul save --keep-optimizer` flag. Resume-from-checkpoint must keep reading
it, so the loader grows one fallback: config.optimizer if present, else the
sidecar. Do NOT migrate existing artifacts in place on a 99%-full disk —
readers must tolerate both layouts, and a soul is re-written on its next save.

Acceptance: a newly saved soul's config header is < 1 MB; parse time for the
cold scan drops under 50 ms for 5 souls; an existing 41 MB soul keeps loading
unchanged (fallback path); a soul saved with --keep-optimizer still resumes
training byte-identically. Benchmark: scripts/benchmark_soul_index.py
(cold_seconds) before/after on a re-saved copy; and a resume-equivalence test
that trains 1 step from a checkpoint saved both ways and compares weights.
title: perf(souls): soul config is 41 MB because it embeds Adam optimizer state — drop it at write time
